items.text: So far, the Cauvery Water Management Authority held 55 meetings and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee held 1 40 meetings. The last meeting of CWMA and CWRC were held on 11.08.2026 at 11.30 a m and 3.00 pm, respectively . In the CWMA and CWRC meetings, the views of Government of Tamil Nadu on issues such as, getting stipulated flows due to Tamil Nadu as per the Orders of the Tribunal and as modified by the Supreme Court Judgement, discussion on new projects including Mekedatu Project of Karnataka,evolving a formula for sharing of distress, Annual Water Account, etc., were strongly placed to safeguard the interest of Farmers in the Cauvery basin. Irrigation Year 2025-2026 In th e irrigation year 20 25-2026, Mettur Dam was opened for irrigation on the scheduled date of 12th June, 2025. Mettur dam reached its full storage capacity of 93.47 TMC, 7 times in the year. The dam was closed for irrigation on 28.01.2026. From 01.06.2025 to 31.03.2026, Tamil Na du has received about 325 TMC at 19 19 Billigundulu. In th e last irrigation year, about 268 TMC of water was supplied for irrigation. Irrigation Year 2026-2027 The live storage of Mettur reservoir at the beginning of the irrigation year 2026 -27, i.e., on 1st June, 2026 was 41.223 TMC. Due to meagre inflows from Karnataka, the live storage on 12 th June, 2026, stood at 41.52 TMC.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Due to meagre inflows from Karnataka, the live storage on 12 th June, 2026, stood at 41.52 TMC. Hence, in this irrigation year 2026-2027, Mettur Dam could not be opened for irrigation on the scheduled date of 12th June, 2026. However, about 1500 cusecs of water is released from the Dam for drinking and environmental uses. Though the South West Monsoon commenced on 04.06.2026, the rainfall received so far is very deficient. Since the flows realised at Billigundulu till 12 th July, 2026 was only 3.26 TMC only, which is only 15.3% of the stipulated flows, the Principal Secretary, WRD addressed the Chairman, CWMA on 14.07.2026, requesting to direct Karnataka to release water to Tamil 20 20 Nadu as per the monthly schedule fixed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Further, in the 139 thCWRC meeting held on 28.07.2026, Tamil Nadu requested the Committee to direct Karnataka to release the due share of Tamil Nadu. The Committee, after reviewing the rainfall and inflows, directed Karnataka to ensure releases from Krishnaraja Sagar and Kabini reservoirs put together so that the flows at the rate of 3500 cusecs are realized at Billigundulu starting from 29.07.2026 (8.00 AM) for the next 15 days, i.e., 4.536 TMC.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: In the 54thmeeting of CWMA held on 30.07.2026, th e Authority endorsed the decision of CWRC, though Tamil Nadu highlighted that even if Karnataka ensures flows as directed, there would be a backlog of 5.410 TMC in the pro -rata share in distress. The Secretary, WRD in letter dated 03.08.2026 addressed to t he Chairman, CWMA, has pointed out that the inflows into the 4 reservoirs of Karnataka have increased considerably from 31.07.2026 and requested to 21 21 revise the pro-rata share due to Tamil Nadu and direct Karnataka to release from KRS and Kabini reservoirs s uch that 26.594 TMC of water is realised at Billigundulu by 12.08.2026. However, Karnataka did not release water as directed by the CWRC/CWMA. The flows realised at Billigundulu from 29.07.2026 to 02.08.2026 were in the range of 144 to 619 cusecs against 3500 cusecs.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: However, Karnataka did not release water as directed by the CWRC/CWMA. The flows realised at Billigundulu from 29.07.2026 to 02.08.2026 were in the range of 144 to 619 cusecs against 3500 cusecs. Hence, as per the instruction of the Hon’ble Chief Minister, Tamil Nadu filed an Application on 03.08.2026 in the Hon’ble Supreme Court, seeking to direct Karnataka to ensure release of waters from its two reservoirs at Kabini and KRS so as to ensure flows at the rate of 3500 cusecs for 15 days, that is, 4.536 TMC, is realised at inter State Border at Billigundulu on or before 12.08.2026 and to direct CWMA to issue appropriate direction to Karnataka to make good the shortfall during the current irrigation year on pro-rata basis, at Billigundulu, for the period from 01.06.2026 to 12.08.2026 of 26. 594 TMC to be released forthwith. 22 22 Since the hydro-meteorological conditions in the catchments upstream of KRS and Kabini have considerably improved, the pro-rata share of Tamil Nadu also needed to be increased.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: 594 TMC to be released forthwith. 22 22 Since the hydro-meteorological conditions in the catchments upstream of KRS and Kabini have considerably improved, the pro-rata share of Tamil Nadu also needed to be increased. Hence, on 07.08.2026 the Secretary to Government, Water Resources Department addressed a letter to the Chairman, CWMA, requesting to convene an emergency meeting of CWMA on 10.08.2026 and to issue a clear and firm direction in the meeting to the State of Karnataka to release water from the KRS and Kabini reservoirs to ensure the receipt of 26.594 TMC of water at Billigundulu by 12.08.2026. Meanwhile, citing deficient rainfall, low reservoir storage and drinking water requirements, the State of Karnataka on29.07.2026 has opposed the recommendation of the CWRC which had directed the release of 3500 Cusecs of water at Billigundulu for a period of 15 days and has sought for the postponement of the distress assessment until the conclusion of the South West Monsoon. 23 23 In response, the Secretary to Government, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu in a letter addressed to the CWMA on 08.08.2026, categorically refuted the contentions raised by Ka rnataka. Tamil Nadu pointed out that in accordance with the final award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal and the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the CWMA has the authority to assess the prevailing distress from time to time and to ensure prop ortionate sharing of water among the basin States.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Accordingly, Tamil Nadu requested the CWMA to reject Karnataka’s appeal and direct the release of the proportionate share of water that is rightfully due to Tamil Nadu. The 140 th meeting of CWRC was held o n 11.08.2026 at 11.30 am. After detailed deliberations, the Committee directed Karnataka to ensure releases from its reservoirs so that the flows at the rate of 12000 cusecs are realised at Billigundulu starting from 12.08.2026 (8.00 am) for the next 15 days. The CWMA, based on Tamil 24 24 Nadu’s request held its 55 th meeting on 11.08.2026 at 3.00 pm. In this meeting, Tamil nadu Member urged that Authority to ddirect Karnataka to release the due pro -rata share of Tamil Nadu upto 27th August, 2026 of 37 TMC However, a fter lengthy deliberations, the Authority endorsed the Committee’s decision. Thus, Tamil Nadu has been continuously monitoring the flows and taking necessary action to build up the storage in Mettur so that it can be opened for irrigation at the earliest. Action taken by Tamil Nadu to prevent Government of Karnataka on its proposal to construct a Dam at Mekedatu Tamil Nadu conveyed its strong objections to Karnataka and Government of India on the proposal of constructing a reservoir at Mekedatu across C auvery immediately, when Karnataka submitted feasibility report of the Mekedatu project, with a capacity of 67.16 TMC, unilaterally. However, the Central Water Commission on 22.11.2018 granted permission to Karnataka for preparation of Detailed Project 25 25 Report (DPR).
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: However, the Central Water Commission on 22.11.2018 granted permission to Karnataka for preparation of Detailed Project 25 25 Report (DPR). Hence, Tamil Nadu on 30.11.2018 filed a Miscellaneous Application in the Supreme Court to restrain Karnataka from preparation of DPR. A Contempt Petition was also filed by Tamil Nadu on 05.12.2018 against the officials concerned. Despite Tamil Nadu’s objections, Karnataka approached the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change for the approval of Terms of Reference (ToR) for Environment Impact Assessment / Environment Management Plan (EIA/EMP) studies. Based on the objections of Tamil Nadu, MoEF & CC informed Karnataka to get the consensus of Tamil Nadu, based on the decision of 25 th EAC meeting held on 19.07.2019. Further, based on the strong objections raised by the Tamil Nadu Member in the Cauvery Water Management Authority meetings to defer discussion of the project, as the matter was sub judice, it was not taken up. In the meanwhile, the National Green Tribunal (Southern Zone) suo mot u took up the issue of construction at Mekedatu Project site 26 26 based on newspaper report and ordered on 21.05.2021 to constitute a Committee to check on any construction activity without obtaining necessary clearance, which was disposed off by the National Green Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi on 17.06.2021, citing that the matter is sub judice. Since Tamil Nadu was not given an opportunity to file its reply, Tamil Nadu filed a Civil Appeal (C.A.No.5608 of 2021) against the above order in the Supreme Court on 11.08.2021. This case is pending.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Since Tamil Nadu was not given an opportunity to file its reply, Tamil Nadu filed a Civil Appeal (C.A.No.5608 of 2021) against the above order in the Supreme Court on 11.08.2021. This case is pending. Further, the Government of Tamil Nadu presented Memoranda to the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 17.06.2021 and the Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti on 06.07.2021, respectively, and requested not to give permission to the proposed Mekedatu reservoir project of Karnataka. A delegation of Leaders of all Legislative Parties of Tamil Nadu also met the Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti on 16.07.2021 and urged the Central Government not to accord any clearance to the Mekedatu 27 27 Project of Karnataka without the concurrence of co-basin States. When it was learnt that Karnatak a had approached the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change for the approval of ToR for EIA/EMP studies, Tamil Nadu filed another Miscellaneous Application with additional documents in the Supreme Court on 27.08.2021, praying to direct CWC to rej ect the DPR for the proposed Mekedatu Project. It was also learnt that Karnataka allocated Rs.1000 Crore in its budget for the year 2022 - 2023, for the Mekedatu Project. The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, on 21.03.2022, strongly condemned this action of Karnataka and unanimously passed resolutions urging the Central Government and the Cauvery Water Management Authority not to accord any clearance to Mekedatu project.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, on 21.03.2022, strongly condemned this action of Karnataka and unanimously passed resolutions urging the Central Government and the Cauvery Water Management Authority not to accord any clearance to Mekedatu project. Subsequently, in the Memoranda presented by the Government of Tamil Nadu to the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 31.03.2022 and on 28 28 26.05.2022 it was inter alia requested to instruct the Ministry of Jal Shakti not to give permission to the proposed Mekedatu Project of Karnataka. In the meanwhile, based on the opinion of the Solicitor General that the Authority has wide powers and it can take up Mekedatu Project for discussion, in the Agenda for 16 th CWMA meeting, Mekedatu Project’s Detailed Project Report was added for discussion. Consequent to that, the Government of Tamil Nadu vide letters dated 04.0 6.2022 and 09.06.2022 addressed CWMA to omit the discussion on Mekedatu Project from the Agenda. Further, Tamil Nadu on 07.06.2022 filed two Applications, praying to restrain CWMA from deliberating / passing any order or direction in regard to the DPR for the proposed Mekedatu Project pending disposal of the Applications already filed by Tamil Nadu.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Further, Tamil Nadu on 07.06.2022 filed two Applications, praying to restrain CWMA from deliberating / passing any order or direction in regard to the DPR for the proposed Mekedatu Project pending disposal of the Applications already filed by Tamil Nadu. Further, the Government of Tamil Nadu wrote a letter to the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 13.06.2022 emphasizing that the CWMA was formed only to implement the Final Award of the Tribunal as modified by the Supreme Court and 29 29 requesting to instruct the Ministry of Jal Shakti to direct the CWMA not to take up Mekedatu Project for discussion, as it is in violation of the Judgement of the Supreme Court. Further, a delegation of leaders of all Legislative Parties, met the Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti on 22.06.2022 and urged to advise the CWMA not to take up Mekedatu DPR for discussion. Tamil Nadu’s requirement was reiterated in the Memorandum presented by the Government of Tamil Nadu to the Hon’ble Union Minister for Jal Shakti on 05.07.2023. When the CWMA in its 28 th meeting held on 01.02.2024 took up Mekedatu Project for discussion, Tamil Nadu vehemently opposed any discussion on Mekedatu project that the matter is sub -judice. After deliberations, the Authority decided to return the DPR of the project back to CWC, and accordingly the DPR was returned back to CWC on 09.02.2024.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: After deliberations, the Authority decided to return the DPR of the project back to CWC, and accordingly the DPR was returned back to CWC on 09.02.2024. In the meanwhile, the Additional Chief Secretary, WRD in his letters dated 07.02.2024 30 30 requested the Secretary, MoJS and the Chairman, CWC not to take any action on Mekedatu project and instruct concerned Directorates of CWC not to entertain any request for processing or giving clearance to the Project, since the matter is sub judice. On the same day, the Additional Chief Secretary, WRD citing the decision taken by EAC on 19.07.2019, requested the Secretary, MoEF&CC to advise the concerned EAC not to entertain any request for grant of ToR. The Chief Secretary to Government of Tamil Nadu also i n letters dated 20.02.2024 addressed to the Secretary, MoJS and the Secretary, MoEF & CC reiterated that the project is not to be examined. Further, the Government of Tamil Nadu in letter dated 23.02.2024, and in the Memorandum dated 25.07.2024 requested t he Hon’ble Union Minister for Jal Shakti to direct the concerned officers in MoJS and CWC not to consider the DPR of Mekedatu project, till Hon’ble Supreme Court decides the issue. 31 31 When it was learnt that Karnataka requested MoEF&CC for approval of ToR, th e Additional Chief Secretary, WRD in letter dated 06.09.2024 requested the Secretary, MoEF & CC to advise the concerned EAC not to entertain any request of Karnataka for grant of ToR.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Government of Tamil Nadu also emphasised the same, citing that the m atter is sub judice in letter dated 09.09.2024 addressed to the Hon’ble Union Minister for Environment, Forest & Climate Change. Due to the strong objections of Tamil Nadu, the Ministry deleted Karnataka’s Mekedatu Project from its list of projects on 03.10.2024. Further, the Hon’ble Union Minister for Environment, Forest & Climate Change, has also replied to the Government of Tamil Nadu on 15.11.2024, wherein he has referred to the decision of 25 th EAC in its meeting on 19.07.2019 that grant of ToR would b e reconsidered after arriving at amicable solution and also stated that Karnataka has not yet submitted the finalized DPR. 32 32 After Karnataka’s repeated insistence, all the Applications connected to Mekedatu issue filed by Tamil Nadu were taken up for hearing on 13.11.2025. Tamil Nadu argued that Mekedatu Project would be harmful to Tamil Nadu; and Karnataka is trying to prevent the flows from uncontrolled catchment, which is against the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. However, Karnataka argued that in 2023 it had ensured more quantity than the quantity directed by the CWMA; and it takes 3 days for the water released from the reservoirs of Karnataka to reach the inter -state border at Billigundulu.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: However, Karnataka argued that in 2023 it had ensured more quantity than the quantity directed by the CWMA; and it takes 3 days for the water released from the reservoirs of Karnataka to reach the inter -state border at Billigundulu. In its Judgement dated 13.11.2025, the Hon’ble Court observed that Mekedatu Project is in premature stage and only the expert body can decide whether this project is as per the Judgement dated 16.02.2018 or not and disposed of all the connected applications, except C. A. No. 5608 of 2021. 33 33 The observation in the above Judgement, especially, in para 29, that every State is free to utilise water allotted to its quota in the manner it finds to be in the best interest of the State, is contrary to the Judgement dated 16.02.2018, wherein it is stated that the alloc ations made should be utilised for the purposes earmarked. Hence, based on the suggestions of the Senior Advocates of Tamil Nadu, a Review Petition was filed on 11.12.2025 in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Further, Tamil Nadu reiterated its request to CWC in letter dated 09.12.2025, detailing how Mekedatu Project would be prejudicial to Tamil Nadu and contrar y to the Judgement dated 16.02.2018.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Further, Tamil Nadu reiterated its request to CWC in letter dated 09.12.2025, detailing how Mekedatu Project would be prejudicial to Tamil Nadu and contrar y to the Judgement dated 16.02.2018. Within a month of the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 13.11.2025, that is, in December 2025, the Union Mi nistry of Jal Shakti unilaterally issued "Guidelines for Assessment of Water Resources Projects in the Cauvery Basin," to pave the way for processing the Mekedatu Project. The Government of Tamil Nadu strongly and continuously opposed these 34 34 guidelines through its letters dated 09.12.2025, 08.01.2026, 06.02.2026, 17.03.2026, 29.04.2026, 23.05.2026, and 09.06.2026. However, the Ministry of Jal Shakti, in its letters dated 20.01.2026, 13.04.2026, and 07.05.2026, repeatedly cited para 29 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court's Judgement dated 13.11.2025 and stated that it would consider the Mekedatu project. Particularly, in its letter dated 07.05.2026, the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti stated that the Central Water Commission has already communicated its comments to Karn ataka on the DPR of Mekedatu project, and stated that further appraisal of the project would be done in compliance to the new guidelines.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Under such circumstance, where the Central Government and the Karnataka Government are attempting to pursue the Mekeda tu project after the Supreme Court dismissed the cases filed against the project by Tamil Nadu, the Government of Tamil Nadu examined the implications of the new guidelines and explored all the options and avenues available before 35 35 Tamil Nadu along with leg al experts. At that time, legal experts pointed out that according to Section 4(1) of the Inter State Water Disputes Act of 1956, a settled matter shall not be reopened. Thus, only after the advice of legal experts, the Government of Tamil Nadu has approached the Central Government on 04.03.2026, requesting it to constitute a new Tribunal. Tamil Nadu reiterated the request for constitution of a Tribunal again on 01.05.2026. In the meanwhile, the Review Petition filed by Tamil Nadu was dismissed by the Hon’b le Supreme Court on 15.04.2026. When the media on 21.05.2026 reported the statement of the Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka about conducting Bhoomi Puja for Mekedatu Project, the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on 25.05.2026, convened a high - level meeting to deliberate on the further course of action in respect of the proposed Mekedatu reservoir project of Karnataka. Based on the discussion, the Hon’ble Chief Minister directed that appropriate legal action be initiated to 36 36 prevent the State of Karnat aka from proceeding with Bhoomi Puja for Mekedatu Project without environmental clearance.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Based on the discussion, the Hon’ble Chief Minister directed that appropriate legal action be initiated to 36 36 prevent the State of Karnat aka from proceeding with Bhoomi Puja for Mekedatu Project without environmental clearance. Further, the Hon’ble Chief Minister, requested the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, in letter dated 26.05.2026 and also on 27.05.2026 when met in person, not to accord any clearance to Mekedatu Project. In this regard, the Principal Secretary, WRD also requested the Secretary, MoJS not to accord any clearance to Mekedatu Project, in letter dated 23.05.2026. As directed by the Hon’ble Chief Minister, an Original Applic ation was filed on 27.05.2026 before the Principal Bench of National Green Tribunal at New Delhi, seeking to restrain the State of Karnataka not to take any steps at the proposed site including the “Bhoomi Puja” for Mekedatu Project, without obtaining mand atory environmental clearance and also to restrain the Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, GoI from granting any permission pending clearance of the inter-State issues. 37 37 A resolution was also passed on 19.06.2026 unanimously, urging the Government of India for the constitution of a new Tribunal, and a copy of the same was sent by the Hon'ble Chief Minister on the very same day in D.O. letter to the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Further, the Hon’ble Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources in letter to the Hon’ble Minister for Jal Shakti dated 24.07.2026 has reiterated the request of Tamil Nadu for the constitution of a Tribunal. In the meanwhile, the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti replied in the Rajya Sabha with respect to Mekedatu that the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 16.02.2018 does not expressly stipulate that Karnataka should obtain the consent of the lower riparian States before constructing a structure across Cauvery. The Hon’ble Chief Minister, took up this matter to the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India in letter dated 28.07.2026, raising serious concerns. Further, he cited the relevant provisions and various paras in the Final Award 38 38 of the Tribunal, and requested to ensure that no statutory or admini strative approval is granted to Mekedatu Project unless it is demonstrably consistent with CWDT Award and the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. Meanwhile, in response to a query raised by a Member of Parliament regarding environmental clearance for the Mekedatu dam project, the Hon’ble Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change replied on 27.07.2026, that neither the Ministry of Jal Shakti nor the Cauvery Water Management Authority has yet granted approval for the DPR of Mekedat u Project and further informed that DPR for Projects received from any basin State would be examined in accordance with the extant Guidelines.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: In response to another Member of Parliament regarding DPR of Mekedatu Project, the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti has also given a similar reply on 03.08.2026. He has further stated that Karnataka has not yet submitted the revised DPR of Mekedatu Project. 39 39 Thus, it is clear that the Central Government would examine the DPR of new projects, if received from t he Cauvery basin States under the new Guidelines. Hence, as ordered by the Hon’ble Chief Minister, Tamil Nadu has filed a Writ Petition in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 03.08.2026, praying to quash the new Guidelines issued by MoJS. Thus, this Government re mains firmly committed to protecting the rights and interests of the people of Tamil Nadu. The Government of Tamil Nadu is taking all necessary actions, including legal action to prevent Karnataka from constructing a Dam at Mekedatu or any other place, in the Cauvery basin of Karnataka, in violation of the Final Order of the Tribunal and the Judgement of the Supreme Court and to safeguard the rights of Tamil Nadu. Suit filed by Karnataka in the Hon’ble Supreme Court against Mettur -Sarabanga LIS, Cauvery – Vaigai – Gundar Link Project & ERM/Modernisation Projects taken up by Government of Tamil Nadu in Cauvery Basin 40 40 The State of Karnataka filed an Original Suit (O.S. No.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: No. 3 of 2021) along with an I.A. in the Supreme Court on 19.07.2021 seeking exclusive right to use surplus waters generated in the Cauvery basin up to inter -state border Billigundulu, over and above 483 TMC and also seeking to restrain Tamil Nadu from executing Mettur Sarabanga Lift Irrigation Scheme, Cauvery-South Vellar link (first phase of Cauvery-Gundar link), construction of check dams, dykes and anicuts, barrages across Cauvery and Kollidam, and Extension, Renovation and Modernization (ERM) of 4 systems, namely, Kattalai High Level Canal System, Rajavoikkal Irrigation System, Noyyal River System and Grand Anicut Canal System in Cauvery basin. Tamil Nadu filed its Written Statement and Reply to the I.A. on 03.01.2022, replying, inter alia, that these projects are either for modernising the irrigation systems or for increasing the efficiency of the systems, or for better commandability or for flood management 41 41 and none of these projects involve development of any new ayacut in Cauvery basin of Tamil Nadu. The cross examination of Karnataka’s 1 st witness was completed on 19.03.2026. The cross examination of the 2nd witness was held on 28.07.2026 and 29.07.2026. Further cross examination is ordered to be held on 19.08.2026 and 20.08.2026.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The cross examination of the 2nd witness was held on 28.07.2026 and 29.07.2026. Further cross examination is ordered to be held on 19.08.2026 and 20.08.2026. Return of non -consumptive use of water drawn for Bangalore water supply sought as per the Judgement of the Supreme Court The Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) considered drinking water requirement of in -basin population only and allocated only 20% of the drinking water drawal as consumptive use. However, the Supreme Court has considered the drinking water r equirement of the entire Bangalore city, two -third of which lies outside Cauvery basin and made an additional allocation of 4.75 TMC as consumptive use to Karnataka. Thus, the balance 80% of the drinking water drawal, that is, non-consumptive 42 42 use, should b e returned to the Cauvery river system as regenerated flows after necessary treatment. Karnataka has not ensured return flows after treatment from the Cauvery waters being supplied in the two -third of Bangalore city, which falls outside Cauvery basin. On t he contrary, Karnataka contends that the return flows/non-consumptive use of waters belongs to it. This issue was raised before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) on various occasions. However, t he CWMA did not issue any direction to the State of Karnataka for ensuring compliance of the decision of Supreme Court or monitor the actual quantum of return flows or its quantity.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: However, t he CWMA did not issue any direction to the State of Karnataka for ensuring compliance of the decision of Supreme Court or monitor the actual quantum of return flows or its quantity. Hence, the Government of Tamil Nadu filed a Miscellaneous Application befo re the Supreme Court on 30.01.2023, praying inter alia to direct Karnataka to ensure that 80% of the flows drawn from Cauvery river and its tributaries for drinking water supply of Bangalore city as 43 43 regenerated flows from domestic use is returned after tre ating the said water, to the Cauvery River system, and CWMA to monitor the quality and quantity of non-consumptive use of drinking water drawn for Bangalore Water Supply returned to Cauvery basin. This Application was heard along with the Applications file d in connection with Mekedatu on 13.11.2025. The Hon’ble Supreme Court ordered to approach CWC and disposed of. Hence, Tamil Nadu in its letter dated 12.12.2025 requested CWC to direct Karnataka to return the quantity of non -consumptive use drinking water drawn for Bangalore Water Supply, to Cauvery basin as per the Judgement. Since there is no response from CWC, the Government of Tamil Nadu in letter dated 19.06.2026 reiterated its request. Action taken by Tamil Nadu in connection with the construction of check dam across Silandhiyar in Pambar (Amaravathy) basin by Kerala 44 44 It was reported in the media in May, 2024 that the Government of Kerala was constructing a check dam across Silandhi river in Amaravathi (Pambar) sub basin of Cauvery basin without obtaining necessary clearances.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Based on the news reports, the National Green Tribunal, Southern Zone (NGT, SZ), suo motu, registered a case (OA No. 181 of 2024). The Chief Secretaries of the States of Kerala & Tamil Nadu, are Respondents. The Government of Tam il Nadu in letter dated 23.05.2024 requested the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Kerala not to proceed with the construction. During the irrigation season 2012-2013, the flows due to Tamil Nadu, as per the Interim 48 48 Order dated 25.06.1991 of CWDT, were not released by Karnataka. Hence, the State of Tamil Nadu filed a Suit (O.S.No.4/2013) against Karnataka in the Hon ’ble Supreme Court of India, claiming damages for the losses caused by Karnataka, to Tamil Nadu due to shortfall in release of stipulated quantity of water, computed as per the pro rata formula, based on the Interim Order of the Tribunal, seeking directions to Karnataka to pay damages of a sum of about Rs.1045.70 crore towards loss of crops, loss of bio mass and loss of power generation, and to pay punitive damages of Rs.1434 crore for deliberate non -compliance of the decision passed by the Tribunal. Cross examination of the 3 witnesses of Tamil Nadu, was over on 28.09.2018. Cross examination of first witness of Karnataka was completed on 30.04.2019. Karnataka filed an IA on 05.06.2026, seeking permission to substitute its second witness along with the Affid avit of the second witness. Tamil Nadu is taking appropriate action in consultation with the Senior Advocate. 49 49 ii. items.text: 49 49 ii. Cauvery River Water Rights This Government will secure Tamil Nadu’s rightful share of Cauvery water as per the 2018 Supreme Court judgment. Immedi ate legal action will be taken against any obstacles in obtaining Tamil Nadu's due share of water. Steps will also be taken to further strengthen Tamil Nadu's rights in the Cauvery Management Authority. Through continuous and effective monitoring, not even a single drop of Tamil Nadu’s rightful share in the Cauvery will be compromised (Vetri Thamizhagam Vision). The Cauvery river is the lifeline of the Cauvery Delta, one of the most productive agricultural regions of Tamil Nadu. Millions of farmers depend u pon the timely release of Cauvery water for irrigation, while several towns and villages rely upon the river for drinking water supply and other domestic requirements. Ensuring the State's rightful share of Cauvery water therefore continues to remain one o f the highest priorities of the Government of Tamil Nadu. 50 50 The Government is steadfastly committed to protecting the rights of Tamil Nadu as determined by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in its judgement dated 16.02.2018. The Water Resources Department continuous ly monitors rainfall, reservoir storages, inflows and releases in the Cauvery basin to assess water availability and to ensure compliance with the monthly release schedule prescribed under the final allocation. The Department actively represents the interests of Tamil Nadu before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) by presenting technical data, reservoir conditions, inflow analysis and irrigation requirements of the Cauvery Delta.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: The Department actively represents the interests of Tamil Nadu before the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) by presenting technical data, reservoir conditions, inflow analysis and irrigation requirements of the Cauvery Delta. Continuous efforts are also undertaken to ensure that Karnataka releases water at Billigundulu in accordance with the monthly schedule prescribed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. In addition to safeguarding the allocated share of water, the Government is pursuing all 51 51 appropriate legal, administrative and technical measures to protect the interests of Tamil Nadu in matters relating to upstream developments, including the proposed Mekedatu Project. The State continues to engage with the Government of India and other competent au thorities to ensure that no project adversely affects the rights and interests of Tamil Nadu or the livelihood of farmers dependent on Cauvery waters. The Government also accords priority to scientific reservoir management, real -time hydrological monitorin g, periodic assessment of water availability and strengthening institutional mechanisms for interstate water management so as to ensure sustainable utilisation of Cauvery waters for irrigation, drinking water supply and ecological requirements. iii. items.text: Cauvery Tec hnical Cell cum Inter – State Waters Wing The Cauvery Technical Cell cum Inter – State Waters Wing is assisting the Government in dealing with all the Inter – State Water 52 52 sharing disputes / issues. This Wing has been functioning since 1990 and provides all technical reports/data and information to the Government required for filing Petitions, Counter petitions, Affidavits, etc., in the Water Disputes Tribunal / Hon’ble Supreme Court and participates in the periodic meeting of the River Water Management Authority, Regulation Committee of Inter State River basin in which Tamil Nadu is a riparian State or stakeholder. This Wing is also dealing with Bills / Acts, Rules and policies related to Water Resources proposed by Central Government and schemes for Inter -linking of Inter-State Rivers and participates in various Committees of the Central Government on these subjects and with the Central Government departments / agencies, viz., National Water Development Agency (NWDA) and Central Water Commission (CWC), Minis try of Jal Shakti, Central Government, etc. This wing also prepares reports on development of water resources of the State. 53 53 Some of the important issues handled by this Wing are Sharing of Cauvery waters, establishing the rights of the State in the Mullai Periyar Dam, obtaining the rightful share of waters from the Parambikulam - Aliyar Project (PAP), Neyyar River irrigation scheme, Pennaiyar and Palar River water disputes.

Mullai Periyar Dam The Periyar Project was executed by virtue of the Lease Deed signed between the Maharaja of Travancore and the Madras Presidency on 29.10.1886. This deed is valid for 999 years with effect from 01.01.1886. About 8,000 acre have been leased for this project. About 2.20 Lakh acre of ayacut area are benefited by this Project in Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Sivagangai and Ramanathapuram Districts and in a yea r, on an average, 22 TMC of water is diverted. Apprehensions were raised about the safety of 54 54 this Dam by certain people of Kerala in the year 1979, though the dam was safe. However, in order to bring the Dam to modern standards, the Central Water Commission suggested certain remedial measures after which the water level could initially be raised to 145 ft. which was not accepted by Kerala. Since the Government of Kerala held the view that the water level in the Dam should be kept at 136 ft. at all times eve n after strengthening, the issue went to the Hon’ble Supreme Court. In the Writ Petitions filed, the Hon’ble Supreme Court pronounced its Judgment on 27.02.2006, which permitted the Government of Tamil Nadu to raise the water level to 142 ft.

items.text: In the Writ Petitions filed, the Hon’ble Supreme Court pronounced its Judgment on 27.02.2006, which permitted the Government of Tamil Nadu to raise the water level to 142 ft. However, the Government of Kerala amended its Kerala Irrigation and Water Conservation Act, 2003, to thwart the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Order and fixed the FRL of Mullai Periyar Dam as 136 ft. In the Suit (O.S.No.3 of 2006) filed by Government of Tamil Nadu against th e amended Act of Kerala, the Hon’ble Supreme Court delivered its Judgment 55 55 on 07.05.2014 and affirmed the Judgment of 2006 and categorically stated that the dam is Hydrologically, Structurally and Seismically safe. Further, Hon’ble Supreme Court held that t he amended Act of Kerala is unconstitutional in so far as Mullai Periyar Dam is concerned. The Hon’ble Court also permitted Tamil Nadu to raise the water level of Mullai Periyar Dam upto 142 ft. and to carry out balance strengthening works, so as to enable Tamil Nadu to restore the FRL + 152 ft. The Hon’ble Supreme Court also stated that the New Dam proposal of Kerala cannot be thrusted upon Tamil Nadu. It also ordered to constitute a Supervisory Committee to periodically inspect the dam to allay the apprehensions of Kerala, though none exists. Water level in the Dam Water level in the Mullai Periyar Dam reached 142 ft. on 21.11.2014, after 35 years, and thereafter on 07.12.2015 and 15.08.2018.

items.text: Water level in the Dam Water level in the Mullai Periyar Dam reached 142 ft. on 21.11.2014, after 35 years, and thereafter on 07.12.2015 and 15.08.2018. It is significant that this historical event took place after 1979. For the 5 th time, the water level reached +142 ft. on 27.12.2022 and the dam is safe in all respects.In the year 2024 -25, the water level of the dam did not cross 132.00 feet due to deficit rainfall in the catchment area of the dam. items.text: Meanwhile, in letter dated 27.11.2025, the Central Minister for Environment, For est and Climate Change has stated that no submission has been received on this matter for consideration by the Standing Committee of the National Wildlife Board. The information given by the Counsel for Kerala in the Hon’ble Supreme Court and the informati on given in the letter by the Hon’ble Central Minister are contradictory. The Chairman, NDSA & Supervisory Committee was addressed on 22.12.2025 in this regard, and requested to direct the Government of Kerala to take necessary action, as the work has been pending for a long time & was further reminded on 23.02.2026, 27.03.2026, 08.04.2026 & 20.07.2026. 75 75 Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation (CDSE) As per Section 38 of the Dam Safety Act, 2021, Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation, shall be conducted within fiv e years from the date of commencement of the Act, for all Dams. This review will be conducted for other Dams in Tamil Nadu. i.e., it has to be completed by December 2026. Thereafter, the Comprehensive Dam Safety Review shall be revived at an interval of 10 years. Prior to this, a similar evaluation of the Mullai Periyar Dam was carried out by the Empowered Committee during 2010 - 12, as per the orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. In the Supervisory Committee meetings, Government of Tamil Nadu emphasised that the safety assessment should not be a hindrance in carrying out the remaining strengthening works, as ordered by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. But Kerala insisted that it should be taken up immediately.

items.text: In the Supervisory Committee meetings, Government of Tamil Nadu emphasised that the safety assessment should not be a hindrance in carrying out the remaining strengthening works, as ordered by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. But Kerala insisted that it should be taken up immediately. The Chairman of the Supervisory 76 76 Committee opined that u ntil then the strengthening works should not be halted. In the 17 th Supervisory Committee (extended) meeting held on 02.09.2024, it was decided that Tamil Nadu will submit the Terms of Reference within two months for the constitution of the Expert Committe e as the Comprehensive Dam Safety Evaluation would take several months. Subsequently, in letter dated 28.10.2024, the Terms of Reference (ToR) was sent to the Chairman, Supervisory Committee. In the 4 th meeting of the Newly constituted Supervisory Committee held on 10.11.2025, as per the decisions taken, the Government of Tamil Nadu recommended a Panel of Experts to conduct the study and sent it to the Chairman of the Supervisory Committee on 01.12.2025. In letter dated 06.01.2026 the Member (Disaster and Resilience), NDSA, New Delhi, constituted a four-member panel with the Chairman. Similarly, an expert committee has been constituted for Parambikulam, Thunakadavu and 77 77 Peruvaripallam Dams on 07.01.2026. Similar expert committees were constituted to conduct integrated dam safety review for other Dams in the State as per the Dam Safety Act 2021.

items.text: Similar expert committees were constituted to conduct integrated dam safety review for other Dams in the State as per the Dam Safety Act 2021. The Government of Tamil Nadu is making all efforts for the rights of Tamil Nadu and the interests of the farmers who depend on the water of Mulla Periyar Dam, by carry ing out the remaining strengthening works and raising the water level in the dam to 152 feet. Construction of a Mega Car Park in the water spread area of Mullai Periyar Dam by the Government of Kerala The proposal of the State of Kerala for construction of a Mega Car Park Complex in water spread area of Mullai Periyar Dam, the National Green Tribunal (Southern Zone), in its Judgment dated 15.11.2017, ordered that since National Tiger Conservation Authority has granted permission, approval under the Forest Conservation Act is not necessary. Against this Judgment, Government of Tamil Nadu has filed Civil Appeals in Hon’ble Supreme Court. 78 78 The Hon’ble Court on 04.12.2017 has ordered that no permanent construction should be carried out by Government of Kerala. A s Government of Kerala has undertaken construction works of permanent nature, Government of Tamil Nadu on 08.05.2019 filed a Contempt Petition in Hon’ble Supreme Court against the concerned officers of Kerala. These matters are pending before Hon’ble Supre me Court. Apart from this, Government of Tamil Nadu on 26.09.2014 has filed a Civil Suit in the Hon’ble Supreme Court against the proposal of Government of Kerala to construct a Mega Car Park, and also to remove the encroachments made by Kerala in the leased area.

items.text: Apart from this, Government of Tamil Nadu on 26.09.2014 has filed a Civil Suit in the Hon’ble Supreme Court against the proposal of Government of Kerala to construct a Mega Car Park, and also to remove the encroachments made by Kerala in the leased area. When this case came up for hearing in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 18.10.2023, the Court was of the opinion that this controversy can be resolved by directing to conduct a joint survey and determination of the precise location of the Mega Car Par k. Further, it was ordered the parties to take instructions and to file 79 79 affidavits by 20 th November 2023 placing on record what according to them is the description of the land, its areas and boundaries and to list the matter on 28th November 2023. Accordingly, Compliance Affidavits were filed by the Government of Tamil Nadu on 18.11.2023 and by the Government of Kerala on 24.11.2023 in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. On 28.11.2023 when the case came up for hearing, it was ordered that the survey as suggested i n terms of the order dated 18 th October, 2023, shall be carried out by the Survey of India or the officers nominated by the Survey of India, with a view to ascertain whether the construction of the Mega Car Park has been made on any part of the property covered by the Periyar Lake Lease Agreement dated 29 th October, 1886.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: A period of three months was granted to the Survey of India to submit its report directly to the Court, from the date on which a copy of the Order is served in its office and the Hon’ble Supreme Court ordered to list the matter for hearing on 11.03.2024. On 80 80 11.03.2024, when the case came up for hearing, the Survey of India submitted its Report in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. As the report was against Tamil Nadu, Counter was filed in the Hon’ ble Supreme Court on 16.04.2024. On that petition, Kerala filed its reply on 09.07.2024, for which rejoinder was filed by the Government of Tamil Nadu on 27.08.2024. As ordered by the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 09.07.2024 and 30.09.2024, the Government of Ta mil Nadu filed Additional documents in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 15.10.2024. Tamil Nadu and Kerala have filed the Admission and Denial of Documents in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 21.11.2024 and 23.11.2024 respectively. Palar River Water Issue The River Palar, which is one of the Inter - State Rivers, originates in Kolar District in Karnataka, traverses through Andhra Pradesh via Chittoor District and runs through Tiruppattur, Vellore, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu District s in Tamil Nadu, before confluence into the Bay of Bengal. The States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are bound by the Inter State – Madras – Mysore, 1892 Agreement.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The States of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are bound by the Inter State – Madras – Mysore, 1892 Agreement. As per Schedule - A of the Agreement, Palar falls under the list of 15 important Inter - State Rivers. When the Government of Andhra Pradesh proposed to construct a Reservoir across Palar river with a capacity of 0.6 TMC at Ganesapuram in Kuppam Taluk of Chittoor District, in violation of the Madras -Mysore Agreement of the year 1892, the Government of Tamil Nadu in the year 2006, filed a Suit in the Hon’ble Supreme Court 84 84 praying to stop the execution of the said project by Andhra Pradesh. Cross -examination of Tamil Nadu witnesses of the Parties were also completed by May 2018. The case is pending in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. In 2024, as there were wide spread reports in the media that the Government of Andhra Pradesh has laid foundation stone for construction of a new dam across Palar river, the Principal Secretary, Water Resources Department, Andhra Pradesh was addressed by Additional Chief Secretary, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu in the letter dated 27.02.2024, not to take up any new work across Palar river as the matter is subjudice. The Government of Tamil Nadu in letter dated 28.02.2024 addressed to the Hon’ble Minister for Water Resources, Andhra Pradesh, requested to instruct the concerned officers of Andhra Pradesh to take immediate action to stop all the related activities with reference to the 85 85 proposal of construction of Dam across the Palar river.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: When the Government of Andhra Pradesh started to increase the height of Checkdams, to repair the existing Checkdams and to construct new Checkdams across Palar river at several places in Chittoor District, Government of Tamil Nadu filed another Suit in the year 2016 in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The Government of Tamil Nadu has also filed Interlocutory Applications (I.A) in the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the years 2017, 2018 and 2019, to restore height of the existing Checkdams to its original level and to allow natural flow due to Tamil Nadu. This matter is also pending in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The Government of Tamil Nadu is taking all necessary steps to protect drinking water needs and irrigation needs of farmers of Tiruppattur, Vellore, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai, Kancheepuram and Chengalpattu districts who depend on the waters of the Palar river. 86 86 vi. Parambikulam - Aliyar Project – Review of Agreement Parambikulam - Aliyar Project, was planned, designed and executed by Government of Tamil Nadu as one of the Second Five Year Plan Projects (1956 - 61), with the consent and co - operation of Government of Kerala for sharing mutual benefits through the utilization of flows in the west flowing rivers of Anamalayar, Nirar, Sholayar, Parambikulam and its tributaries Peruvaripallam, Thunakadavu and the Palar and Aliyar flowing in the plains and the streams flowing into them, for generation of Hydro Electric Power, irrigation, drinking water supply, industrial use and other purposes.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: An Agreement between Governments of Kerala and Tamil Nadu was entered into on 29.05.1970 with retrospective effect from 09.11.1958. The Pollachi, Palladam, Udumalaipettai and Dharapuram Taluks in Coimbatore and Tiruppur Districts are benefitt ed. Palakkad and Trichur Districts of Kerala State are also benefited. This Agreement was due for review on 09.11.1988 and thereafter once in 30 years. For this, both 87 87 Governments exchanged documents and also exchanged their respective views. For the review of the Agreement, so far 28 Meetings at various levels were held between Tamil Nadu and Kerala. In the last Inter State meeting held through Video Conferencing on 17.09.2021, all the issues related to Parambikulam - Aliyar Project including Anamalayar Project and Nirar - Nallar Project were discussed, which are briefed as below: Diversion of 2.5 TMC of water from Anamalayar to Tamil Nadu & Nirar - Nallar Multipurpose Straight Cut Scheme There is a provision to divert 2.5 TMC of water from Anamala yar, in the Original Agreement. Contending that its Idamalayar Project has not been completed, Kerala has not yet given consent for the above diversion. A Supplementary Agreement will suffice for this purpose.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Contending that its Idamalayar Project has not been completed, Kerala has not yet given consent for the above diversion. A Supplementary Agreement will suffice for this purpose. However, after discussion in the Inter - State meetings held on 12.12.2019 at Chennai, 11.09.2020 at Thiruvananthapuram and through 88 88 Video Conference on 17.09.2021, Kerala has expressed its willingness to consider the proposal of Tamil Nadu for constructing a weir across Italiar, a tributary of Anamalaya r for diverting 2.5 TMC to Tamil Nadu. The Nirar - Nallar Multipurpose Straight Cut Scheme envisages formation of a Reservoir about 7 TMC capacity across Nallar, a tributary of Palar in Bharathapuzha basin, for conveyance of water from Upper Nirar Weir acr oss Nirar River directly to Nallar by means of a tunnel for irrigation and also utilize it for generation of Hydro-Electric power. Tamil Nadu is pressing for Nirar – Nallar Multipurpose Straight cut scheme to the present circuitous route i.e., from Upper Nirar to Sholayar Reservoir, then to Parambikulam Reservoir and then through the contour canal to Thirumurthy Reservoir, to reduce water loss. In the Inter -State meetings held on 12.12.2019 at Chennai, 11.09.2020 at Thiruvananthapuram and through Video Conference on 17.09.2021, the Nirar - Nallar 89 89 Project was deliberated. Technical details and data pertaining to Nirar - Nallar Scheme proposal of Tamil Nadu was sent to Kerala on 08.02.2021.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Technical details and data pertaining to Nirar - Nallar Scheme proposal of Tamil Nadu was sent to Kerala on 08.02.2021. In Video Conference meeting held on 17.09.2021, Kerala put forth its d emand for an increased share of water, about 2.5 to 3 TMC at Manacadavu Weir. As decided in the Inter State meeting held on 17.09.2021, Tamil Nadu constituted a Technical Sub Committee on 01.10.2021, to deliberate with regards to benefits to both the States and sort out technical issues of both the Projects. Kerala’s response is awaited. The matter is under correspondence. The Technical Sub Committee has conducted two meetings, on 20.10.2021 and 03.08.2022 and discussed about the technical issues which are to be sorted with Kerala appropriately. After getting consent of Kerala, Detailed Project Reports will be prepared and after obtaining the necessary clearances, the Anamalayar and Nirar - Nallar projects would be executed. 90 90 The Government of Tamil Nadu, in letter dated 28.09.2023 informed the Hon’ble Minister for Water Resources, Kerala that a meeting may be convened at the Chief Secretary level to discuss all the issues and then the Hon'ble Chief Ministers of Kerala and Tamil Nadu may hold discussion. Thi s was followed by correspondences between both Governments, in 2024 & 2025, to conduct Hon’ble Ministers’ level meeting. The Secretary, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu in letters dated 14.01.2026 & 23.02.2026 proposed a meeting at Hon’ ble Minsters’ level to discuss on Inter-State issues. The response from Kerala is awaited.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Secretary, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu in letters dated 14.01.2026 & 23.02.2026 proposed a meeting at Hon’ ble Minsters’ level to discuss on Inter-State issues. The response from Kerala is awaited. The Government of Tamil Nadu is pursuing the issues with the Government of Kerala to complete the review of the PAP Inter State Agreement and to execute the Anamalay ar and Nirar - Nallar Projects considering the interest of the farmers of Tamil Nadu. 91 91 Irrigation year 2025-2026 In this water year, depending on the inflows in Aliyar sub basin and the Tamil Nadu Sholayar Reservoir, water is being supplied to Kerala, as per the PAP Agreement, at Manacadavu weir and Kerala Sholayar Reservoir. At Manacadavu weir for the period from July 2025 to March 2026, 13.505 TMC of water has been supplied to Kerala which is in excess of 7.250 TMC to be supplied in the entire water year 2025-26, as per Agreement. At Kerala Sholayar Reservoir also, for the period from July 2025 to March 2026, 14.528 TMC of water has been supplied. Upto March 2026, the utilisation at Kerala Sholayar Reservoir powerhouse was 10.970 TMC and live storage was 2.576 TMC, totalling 13.546 TMC, which is in excess of 12.3 TMC for entire water year as per Agreement. vii.

items.text: Neyyar Irrigation Project The Neyyar Irrigation Project was planned by the Travancore - Cochin Government in two stages during the 2 nd Five-Year Plan (19 56–61) and constructed. Thereafter, due to the States 92 92 Re-organisation in 1956, a portion of the ayacut localised to be served by this project to the extent of 9,200 acre lying in Vilavancode Taluk was transferred to Tamil Nadu and forms part of Kanniyakumari District. The canal works in Vilavancode area required to feed this ayacut were executed by the Government of Tamil Nadu with the concurrence of the Central Government and the Government of Kerala. The project has been in operation since 1965. The Government of Kerala abruptly stopped the supply of water in March 2004. Even though bilateral discussions were held several times to release water to Tamil Nadu, no solution could be found.Hence, in the year 2012, Government of Tamil Nadu filed an Original Sui t in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. The cross -examination of Tamil Nadu’s witness is over. The cross - examination of 2 witnesses on behalf of State of Kerala concluded on 12.09.2024 and 02.05.2025. Meanwhile, the Government of Tamil Nadu has filed two Interloc utory Applications in the Hon’ble Supreme Court, one seeking a copy of 93 93 the Neyyar Irrigation Project Report, on 10.01.2025 and the other seeking an interim order to release water into the Neyyar Left Bank Canal, on 12.02.2025.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The State of Kerala filed a Reply Affidavit on 11.12.2025 stating that neither the copy nor the original of the said project report of the Neyyar Irrigation Project formulated in 1955 is available as of now. This case is expected to be listed soon in the Hon’ble Supreme Court for final arguments. The Tamil Nadu Government is taking all efforts to get water from the Neyyar Dam, to safeguard the interests of the farmers in Vilavancode Taluk and to protect the rights of Tamil Nadu. viii. Repairs to Shenbagavalli Anicut Shenbagavalli Anicut is a diversion Anicut built at the junction of two streams viz., Puliampattithodu and Chokkampattithodu in the head reach of Periyar Basin lying in Kerala State limits just to the west of Tamil Nadu border. This 94 94 anicut is in existence for more than 200 years and it diverts flows to mainly two Tanks namely Kulashekharaperi and Rasingeperi in Sivagiri Taluk of Tenkasi District through a channel, namely, Kanyamathagu channel, which is 4,400 ft. (1341m) long, which supply water to a group of Tanks. About 10,924 acre in Tenkasi and Virudhunagar Districts are being irrigated. In order to carry out the repairs to the Shenbagavalli Anicut, the Government of Tamil Nadu is continuously requesting Government of Kerala, to give its consent.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: About 10,924 acre in Tenkasi and Virudhunagar Districts are being irrigated. In order to carry out the repairs to the Shenbagavalli Anicut, the Government of Tamil Nadu is continuously requesting Government of Kerala, to give its consent. This issue was also ta ken up during the talks with Kerala at Additional Chief Secretary level on 12.12.2019, 11.09.2020 and 17.09.2021. A writ petition (W.P. 12922/2019) was filed before the Madurai Bench of the Hon’ble Madras High Court seeking early execution of the renovation works of the Shenbagavalli Dam and the Kanyamathagu Canal. The Government of Tamil Nadu filed its counter affidavit in this regard. On 02.07.2025, the Hon’ble Madurai 95 95 Bench of the Madras High Court dismissed the case, stating that the said dam is situate d within the Kerala boundary. To protect the welfare of the farmers, the Government of Tamil Nadu is taking all necessary steps to obtain the consent of the Kerala Government for carrying out the renovation works of the Shenbagavalli Dam and the Kanyamathagu Canal at the earliest and also will take up this issue for discussion in the forthcoming Interstate meetings. ix. Pennaiyar River Water Issue River Pennaiyar originates at Nandidurg in Karnataka and flows through States of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Union Territory of Puducherry before confluence into the Bay of Bengal. Pennaiyar river is an Inter-State river and forms part of the Madras - Mysore Agreement of 1892.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Pennaiyar river is an Inter-State river and forms part of the Madras - Mysore Agreement of 1892. Government of Tamil Nadu, in 2018, has filed a Suit (O.S. No. 1 of 2018) and an Interlocutory Application before the Hon’ble Supreme Court against Government 96 96 of Karnataka which is undertaking the works of construction of Dam across the Markandeya river, a tributary of Pennaiyar and diversion structures to divert water from River Penna iyar in violation of the Madras -Mysore Agreement of 1892. Hon’ble Supreme Court in its order dated 14.11.2019 for the Interim Petition (I.A.No.95384/2019) filed by Tamil Nadu granted liberty to Tamil Nadu to make an appropriate application to Central Gove rnment for constitution of a Tribunal for adjudication of Pennaiyar river Water Dispute. Government of Tamil Nadu on 30.11.2019 has approached the Central Government, Ministry of Jal Shakti to constitute a Tribunal. Further, Government of Tamil Nadu on 16. 12.2019 filed an Interlocutory Application (I.A. No. 193417 of 2019) in the Hon’ble Supreme Court for maintenance of status quo of the projects of Karnataka. In January 2020, Ministry of Jal Shakti, Central Government set up a Negotiation Committee headed by the Chairman, Central 97 97 Water Commission. No decision could be reached in the two meetings of the Negotiation Committee. Subsequently, it submitted the Final Report on 31.07.2020, in favour of constitution of the Tribunal.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: No decision could be reached in the two meetings of the Negotiation Committee. Subsequently, it submitted the Final Report on 31.07.2020, in favour of constitution of the Tribunal. Tamil Nadu Government since th en requested Ministry of Jal Shakti on 21.11.2020, 19.02.2021 and 29.06.2021 for early constitution of Tribunal and reiterated the request in the Memorandum presented by the Government of Tamil Nadu to Hon’ble Central Minister of Jal Shakti on 06.07.2021. Secretary, Department of Water Resources, Minister of Jal Shakti convened a meeting with Additional Chief Secretaries of basin States, on 01.09.2021 and the issue was discussed. A meeting for mutual discussions between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka along with Minister of Jal Shakti was suggested. Karnataka opposed on 13.10.2021, the constitution of Tribunal. Government of Tamil Nadu reiterated to Ministry of Jal Shakti on 01.11.2021, 20.12.2021, 98 98 11.03.2022 and 09.05.2022, to constitute the Tribunal early. As th e constitution of Tribunal by the Central Government, was getting delayed, an Additional Affidavit was filed in the Hon’ble Supreme Court, by Tamil Nadu, on 15.07.2022, requesting to give directions to the MoWR, Government of India. The Government of Indi a filed an Affidavit on 14.12.2022 requesting for 6 months’ time to constitute the Tribunal. The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 14.12.2022 directed that the Tribunal be constituted within three months.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Government of Indi a filed an Affidavit on 14.12.2022 requesting for 6 months’ time to constitute the Tribunal. The Hon’ble Supreme Court vide its order dated 14.12.2022 directed that the Tribunal be constituted within three months. The Government of Tamil Nadu citing the order of the Hon’ble Supreme Court requested the Ministry of Jal Shakti on 19.02.2023 to constitute the Tribunal early. In the Petition filed by the Central Government in the Hon’ble Supreme Court on 28.03.2023 and when it was taken up for hearing in the H on’ble Supreme Court on 99 99 02.05.2023, 04.07.2023 and 03.10.2023, the Central Government said that it is considering setting up a Tribunal in the petitions and hearings filed in the Hon’ble Supreme Court. When the case came up for hearing in the Hon’ble Supr eme Court on 23.01.2024, on the request of the Central Government, the Hon’ble Supreme Court directed the Jal Shakti Ministry to set up a new negotiating committee citing Section 4(1) of the River Water Act, 1956 and to submit the Report on the outcome, within 3 months of the constitution of the Committee. The MoJS, vide, Office Memorandum dated 07.02.2024, constituted the 2 nd Negotiation Committee, headed by - Chairman, CWC with Members from the co -basin States & from the Ministry of Agri culture, Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, Ministry of Jal Shakti and Irrigation Management Organization ( IMO).
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Committee was directed to submit its Report within 45 days from the date of issue of Office Memorandum. 100 100 The 2 nd Negotiation Committee on Pennaiyar issue held 9 meetings, viz., on 21.02.2024, 27.03.2024, 22.04.2024, 22.05.2024, 02.07.2024, 08.08.2024, (VC meeting on 16.08.2024), 29.08.2024, 20.09.2024, and 28.09.2024. The Committee visited upper Pennaiyar basin area of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu from 08.06.2024 to 10.06.2024. The request to constitute the Tribunal early was reiterated in the Memorandum presented by the Government of Tamil Nadu to Hon’ble Central Minister of Jal Shakti on 25.07.2024. The 2 nd Negotiation Committee s ubmitted its Final Report to the MoJS for further consideration on 30.09.2024. On 02.01.2025, the Central Government filed a petition along with the report of the 2 nd Negotiation Committee of Pennaiyar. A meeting under the Chairpersonship of Secretary, Dept. of WR, RD & GR, GoI with the Additional Chief Secretaries of concerned basin States was held on 03.03.2025 (hybrid mode) 101 101 and the Report of the 2nd Negotiation Committee for Pennaiyar River Water Dispute was deliberated.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: A meeting of the Hon’ble Ministers for Water Resources of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Puducherry and Tamil Nadu under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Jal Shakti, Government of India, to discuss on the Report of the 2 nd Negotiation Committee on Pennaiyar river Water Dispute, was sch eduled on 18.03.2025 and thereafter postponed due to the refusal of the Government of Tamil Nadu to participate and the Government of Tamil Nadu insisted only on the constitution of a Water Dispute Tribunal. Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Government requested the M oJS repeatedly in letters dated 14.02.2025, 15.03.2025, 28.03.2025, and the Government of Tamil Nadu addressed the Hon’ble Minister of Jal Shakti, Government of India in letters dated 19.05.2025 & 16.10.2025 to take immediate action for constituting a 102 102 Tribunal for the resolution of the Pennaiyar dispute without any further delay. Meanwhile, the Government of India filed an Affidavit dated 07.10.2025, and filed the status that the meeting at Minister’s level was postponed indefinitely. Also, in the Affidavit, the Government of India had not given any commitment on the constitution of the Tribunal. The Hon’ble Central Minister, Jal Shakti on 30.10.2025, in response to previous letter of Government of Tamil Nadu dated 19.05.2025, stated that the Pennaiyar matt er is under consideration of the Ministry and appropriate action will be taken as deemed, considering all aspects.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: The Hon’ble Supreme Court pronounced its Judgment on 02.02.2026, wherein, the Hon’ble Court directed the Central Government to issue an appropriate notification in the Official Gazette and to constitute a Water Disputes Tribunal for the adjudication of the Pennaiyar water dispute 103 103 within a period of one month from the date of the Judgment and disposed the case. Subsequently, the Tamil Nadu Gov ernment requested the MoJS in letters dated 05.02.2026 & 04.03.2026, that the Tribunal, which the Central Government is mandated by section 4(1) of Act 1956, be constituted without delay. The Government of India on 06.04.2026 filed an IA in the Hon’ble Sup reme Court, in the O.S. No. 1 of 2018, seeking 6 months’ time for compliance of the Judgment dated 02.02.2026 and the gazette notification of the constitution of the Tribunal. A reply to the Application to Government of India will be filed by Government of Tamil Nadu praying to direct the Central Government to constitute the Tribunal at the earliest and in any event within a further period of maximum of four weeks. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, granted six months’ time to the Central Government, to implement t he Judgement dated 02.02.2026, 104 104 vide its order dated 08.05.2026. The constitution of Tribunal is getting delayed. The Central Government on 08.07.2026 filed an application in the Hon’ble Court seeking clarification on referring the Pennaiyar river water di spute to the existing Mahadayi Water Dispute Tribunal instead of constituting a new Tribunal.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: The constitution of Tribunal is getting delayed. The Central Government on 08.07.2026 filed an application in the Hon’ble Court seeking clarification on referring the Pennaiyar river water di spute to the existing Mahadayi Water Dispute Tribunal instead of constituting a new Tribunal. The response of Tamil Nadu to above application filed on 11.08.2026. The Government of Tamil Nadu is taking all necessary action to protect the interests of the farmers of Pennaiyar basin. x. Godavari - Krishna - Pennar - Palar – Cauvery Link The Government of Tamil Nadu is continuously urging Central Government and the Special Committee for Inter linking of rivers formed by the Central Government as per the Judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, dated 27.02.2012 to implement the inter -linking of Peninsular rivers, viz., Mahanad hi - Godavari - Krishna - Pennar - Palar - Cauvery - Vaigai – Gundar, for which National Water Development Agency prepared Feasibility Report in 2004. 105 105 Anticipating this link project, Government of Tamil Nadu, as early as in 2008, took up the construction of Kattalai Barrage across Cauvery and completed it in 2014. In the meanwhile, as the finalisation of Mahanadi -Godavari link is getting delayed , National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has decided to implement the Godavari – Krishna – Pennar - Cauvery link in Phase-I and prepared Detailed Project Report for the same in April 2021 and sent to concerned States for their views.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: Tamil Nadu has requested for enhancing the quantum of water proposed to be transferred to Tamil Nadu from 84 TMC to 200 TMC in Phase -I itself, since it is a water deficit State and to take up the link at a higher contour and terminate it at Cauvery (Kattalai Barrage) instead of at Cauvery (Grand Anicut), as it will be helpful to supply water to the needy areas for optimum utilization of water. Meanwhile, the Government of Tamil Nadu presented a Memorandum to the Hon’ble Prime Minister on 17.06.2021, among others, 106 106 requested to finalise the Detailed Project Report for this project incorporating the request of Tamil Nadu and take up the work on priority basis, so that Southern States could be benefited from the inter basin transfer of surplus / flood water which was also reiterate d by the Government of Tamil Nadu in his Memorandum presented to the Hon’ble Central Minister of Jal Shakti on 06.07.2021. For the implementation of this link, NWDA conducted five consultation meetings with the concerned States for a consensus building. Whereas, Tamil Nadu in the 3 rd consultation meeting made a presentation on the benefits of taking the link canal at a higher contour. Against the observations of the concerned Party States on the availability of surplus water in Godavari, the Central Water Commission opined that about 4000 MCM of water would be available for diversion to the southern basins. Meanwhile, Central Government in the Budget speech for 2022 -2023 has informed that once a consensus is reached among the 107 107 beneficiary States for this pro ject, it will provide support for its implementation.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: Meanwhile, Central Government in the Budget speech for 2022 -2023 has informed that once a consensus is reached among the 107 107 beneficiary States for this pro ject, it will provide support for its implementation. In the 36 th Annual General meeting of the NWDA Society, held on 13.12.2022 at New Delhi, the Government of Tamil Nadu requested to keep diversion from Godavari as 7000 MCM (247 TMC) as proposed in Detai led Project Report prepared by NWDA in 2021 and take the termination point of the link canal to Kattalai Barrage instead of at Grand Anicut by justifying the need to take up the link canal at a higher contour. The Government of Tamil Nadu, further requested to increase the allocation of water from Godavari – Cauvery link project to the State of Tamil Nadu. The Additional Chief Secretary, Water Resources Department also reiterated the views put forth by the Government of Tamil Nadu. Hon’ble Central Minister for Jal Shakti suggested to conduct a meeting with NWDA officials exclusively to deliberate on these issues and arrive a suitable decision. 108 108 In the 17 th meeting of Task Force Committee of NWDA held on 06.03.2023 at Hyderabad, Tamil Nadu has requested to enhance diversion of 4000 MCM to 7000 MCM from Godavari and take the termination point of the link canal to Kattalai Barrage instead of at Grand Anicut. The Chairman of Task Force Committee has requested States of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to give concu rrence for Godavari and Cauvery Link Project.

items.text: The Chairman of Task Force Committee has requested States of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to give concu rrence for Godavari and Cauvery Link Project. In the 13 th Standing Committee meeting of Southern Zonal Council was held on 05.05.2023 in Chennai. Tamil Nadu reiterated its views and requested to get the consensus of the concerned States for early implementation of this project. The Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Tamil Nadu discussed with the Director, NWDA on 18.08.2023 at Chennai regarding the Godavari – Cauvery link and also the proposal to take up link the canal at a higher elevation across the Palar and terminated at the Kattalai Barrage was discussed. NWDA requested Tamil Nadu to furnish the details regarding the link 109 109 canal terminated at Kattalai barrage early for the preparation of Detailed Project Report for Somasila – Kattalai link canal. The technical details were furnished by the Chief Engineer, Plan Formulation to NWDA. NWDA has conducted its 5 th consultation meeting with the concerned States on 10.11.2023 at Hyderabad. Tamil Nadu requested to get the consent from the concerned Party States for concluding the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to finalize the Detailed Project Report of the Godavari – Cauvery link project. The 21st Special Committee for Interlinking of Rivers meeting was held at New Delhi on 14.12.2023. The Additional Chie f Secretary, Water Resources Department, Tamil Nadu conveyed the support of Tamil Nadu for the Godavari – Cauvery link project and asked to obtain consensus from the party States for the early implementation of this link.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
