items.text: The Additional Chie f Secretary, Water Resources Department, Tamil Nadu conveyed the support of Tamil Nadu for the Godavari – Cauvery link project and asked to obtain consensus from the party States for the early implementation of this link. In the above circumstances, NWDA has prepared the revised DPR of Godavari - Krishna 110 110 – Pennar – Manimuktanadhi River link in December 2023 and circulated to the concerned States for comments. As requested by Tamil Nadu, in the revised DPR, the 1 st phase of the project is to take the link c anal to a higher contour after crossing the Palar Dusimamandur tank and linked it with Manimuktanadhi which is (south of Cauvery – Kattalai barrage) the tributary of Vellar. Water diverted from Godavari is 148 TMC and allocation to Tamil Nadu is 41 TMC. Out of this, 17.2 TMC have been allocated to Tamil Nadu for irrigation and 9.4 TMC for drinking water needs and 12.4 TMC for industrial use. 10.1 TMC has been provided to Greater Chennai for drinking and industrial usage and water losses 2 TMC The Government of Tamil Nadu has sent comments to the National Water Development Agency on 06.03.2024 to terminate the link canal near Ayyar River (upstream of Kattalai Barrage) and to provide 200 TMC of water to Tamil Nadu during the second and third phase of the Godav ari-Cauvery link canal when the diversion from Brahmaputra 111 111 and Mahanadi link takes place from Mahanadi and Himalayan rivers.

items.text: NWDA has prepared the draft Memorandum of Agreement for implementation of Godavari (Inchampalli Barrage) – Cauvery Link Project and sent to the concerned States for comments. On 11.06.2024, the Government of Tamil Nadu sent comments to the National Water Development Agency for consideration. Further, the Government of Tamil Nadu in the Memorandum presented to the Hon’ble Central Mi nister of Jal Shakti on 25.07.2024, requested among others to instruct the Ministry of Jal Shakti and concerned officers of NWDA to take proactive action to get the consensus of the States so as to enable to implement the Godavari – Cauvery link on priority basis, so that Southern States benefited from the inter basin transfer of surplus / flood water. The Government of Tamil Nadu has repeatedly reiterated the need for the expeditious implementation of this interlinking project on priority basis in the 6 th Consultation 112 112 meeting held on 22.08.2025, 75 th Governing Council Meeting of NWDA held on 01.10.2025, 9th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and 24 th meeting of the Special Committee on Interlinking of Rivers (SCILR) held on 23.12.2025. The Principal Secretary to Government, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu participated in the 25 th Special Committee of ILR Meeting held on 15.07.2026.

items.text: The Principal Secretary to Government, Water Resources Department, Government of Tamil Nadu participated in the 25 th Special Committee of ILR Meeting held on 15.07.2026. The Hon’ble Minister of Tamil Nadu wrote a letter on 03.08.2026 to Hon’ble Minister for Water Resources, Andrapr adesh requesting to take appropriate action for giving the concurrence of Andrapradesh to enable National Water Development Agency to execute the Godavarai - Cauvery Link project. The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu wrote a letter on 0 5.08.2026 to Hon’ ble Prime Minister of India requesting to direct the Ministry of JalShakti and the NWDA to: 113 113 i. expedite consultations with the stakeholder States and facilitate an early consensus on the outstanding issues; ii. finalise the DPR for extending the link up to the Ka ttalai Barrage across the river Cauvery; iii. accord priority to the project and take it up for implementation asa National Project on a fast-track basis; and iv. consider establishing a dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle for its coordinated and time-bound execution and declare the project as a project of national importance. The Government of Tamil Nadu is continuously taking all steps to implement this link project through National Water Development Agency and Special Committee on Inter Linking of Rivers and the Ce ntral Government, to alleviate water scarcity in the state.

items.text: The Government of Tamil Nadu is continuously taking all steps to implement this link project through National Water Development Agency and Special Committee on Inter Linking of Rivers and the Ce ntral Government, to alleviate water scarcity in the state. The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Naduhas proposed to insist the necessity to implement the Godavari - Krishna - Pennar - Palar – 114 114 Cauvery Link expeditiously during the 31 st Southern Zonal Counci l Meeting under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Union Minister for Home Affairs to be held on 20.08.2026 at Mahabalipuram. xi. Pamba - Achankovil - Vaippar Link National Water Development Agency in 1994 prepared a feasibility report for the Pamba – Achankovil - Vaippar Link Project, which envisages diversion of 22 TMC of surplus water of Pamba and Achankoil Rivers of Kerala to Tamil Nadu to irrigate an ayacut of 91,400 Ha. in Sankarankoil, Kovilpatti, Sivagiri, Srivilliputhur, Rajapalayam, Sathur and Tenkasi Taluks of Tamil Nadu, which will also help to generate power of 500 MW to Kerala. Even though the Government of Tamil Nadu gave its concurrence for preparing the Detailed Project Report, Government of Kerala is not in favour of this project. Tamil Nadu has been continuously requesting Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India and National Water Development Agency to prepare the Detailed 115 115 Project Report for this link project in all meetings of Special Committee constituted for implementing the Inter Linking of R ivers project.

items.text: Tamil Nadu has been continuously requesting Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India and National Water Development Agency to prepare the Detailed 115 115 Project Report for this link project in all meetings of Special Committee constituted for implementing the Inter Linking of R ivers project. Even during the Special Committee meeting, held on 12.11.2021 at New Delhi, Tamil Nadu citing the heavy flood flows in 2021 in Pamba and Achankoil Rivers of Kerala, requested National Water Development Agency to prepare the Detailed Project Report for Pamba – Achankoil – Vaippar Link project, so as to implement this link speedily, as this link is beneficial to Kerala also, in effective flood management. In the 74 th Governing Body meeting held on 03.12.2024, Tamil Nadu emphasized the need for the Pamba - Achankoil - Vaippar link project since Vaippar basin in Tamil Nadu is a deficit basin and requested to pursue the project. The Government of Tamil Nadu is taking all efforts through the National Water Development Agency, meetings of Special Committee for Inter Linking of Rivers and Central Government for the implementation of this Project. 116 116 xii. Pandiyar – Punnampuzha Project Pandiyar, Punnampuzha and Cholatipuzha are tributaries of the Inter State River Chaliyar. These tributaries originate from the high peaks of Nilgiris hills in Tamil Nadu and flows west into Kerala and empties into the Arabian Sea.

items.text: These tributaries originate from the high peaks of Nilgiris hills in Tamil Nadu and flows west into Kerala and empties into the Arabian Sea. An understanding was reached between Tamil Nadu and Kerala in the year 1965 to implement the (3x50 MW) Pandiyar - Punnampuzha Hydro -Electric Scheme at Karakotapuzha in Tamil Nadu and 105 MW at Putheripallam in Kerala which envisages utilization of 14 TMC water, out of the Annual average yield of 27.6 TMC, generated from the catchment area of Pandiyar and Punnampuzha Rivers in Tamil Nadu. The Central Planni ng Commission approved this project in 1968. There was no diversion of water, suggested in this proposal. Based on the representation from the ryots of Bhavani Sub basin, the Government of Tamil Nadu directed to discontinue the preparation 117 117 works of the Pr oject and to study the feasibility of diverting the Pandiar -Punnampuzha water eastwards into the Moyar River and from there to Lower Bhavani Reservoir in Erode District. Accordingly, the above proposal was investigated and found feasible. In 2006, a Project was prepared by the TNEB and sent to Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) for the concurrence of the Government of Kerala. However, Kerala did not give its nod for the modified proposal. In the inter State meeting held between the Chief Ministers on 25.

In the inter State meeting held between the Chief Ministers on 25. 09.2019 at Thiruvananthapuram, it was decided to constitute a committee comprising of 5 members at the Secretary level of both the States to discuss and advise the respective Governments on implementing the Pandiyar - Punnampuzha Scheme. In continuation of that inter -State meeting was held on 11.09.2020 at Thiruvananthapuram and a meeting by the Committee was held by Video Conference on 17.09.2021. 118 118 In the last meeting Kerala indicated to consider Tamil Nadu’s proposal and it was decided to constitute a Technical Sub Committee to sort out the technical aspects of the proposal and the same has been constituted on 01.10.2021. As announced in the Demand for Grants for the year 2021 -2022 the Government accorded Administrative Sanction for the work of Conducting S urveying & Levelling operation for preparation of feasibility report for the multipurpose Pandiyar – Punnampuzha Project for an amount of Rs.9.00 Lakh. After conducting preliminary investigation and surveying works, feasibility report has been prepared. Further, the Government of Tamil Nadu has suggested holding a bilateral discussion in Chennai soon on the Pandiyar - Punnambuzha and other related projects. The response of the State of Kerala in this regard is awaited.

Krishna Water Supply Project An Agreement was signed among the States of Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh on 14.04.1976, in which each State agreed to spare 5 TMC of water from Krishna basin to supply 15 TMC of water to Greater Chennai through the State of Andhra Pradesh. As per the Inter -State Agreement the Government of Andhra Pradesh has to deliver 12 TMC of water at Tamil Nadu Border every year, excluding evaporation loss of 3 TMC of water as below: 1st spell - July to October (4 Months) : 8 TMC 2nd spell - January to April (4 Months) : 4 TMC 120 120 Thus, a total of 12 TMC has to be realized by Tamil Nadu at the Zero point in a water year. Krishna Water is being supplied to Greater Chennai from 1996. During the water year 2025-26, 4.890 TMC of water realized. A total of 120.763 TMC of water has been realiz ed by Tamil Nadu from 1996 to 31.03.2026.

Steps are being taken to ensure that the officials of both the State Governments share certain statistics to calculate the expenditure to be provided to the Andhra Pradesh Government by the Tamil Nadu Government. 121 121 4. Rivers – Lifeline of Civilization i. Clean Rivers The three major rivers of Tamil Nadu, namely Cauvery, Vaigai and Thamirabarani, have been destroyed due to non -compliance with the appropriate environmental regulations for industries. The Government will take firm measures to prevent this. The discharge of textile industry waste into rivers from regions such as Erode and Tiruppur will be completely prevented, and alternative waste management arrangements will be implemented.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Government will take firm measures to prevent this. The discharge of textile industry waste into rivers from regions such as Erode and Tiruppur will be completely prevented, and alternative waste management arrangements will be implemented. Riverfront parks will also be developed along the Cauvery in Tlruchirappalli, the Vaigai in Madurai, and the Tamirabarani in Tirunelveli. – (Vetri Thamizhagam Vision) The Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to restoring the ecological integrity of the State's rivers through integrated river rejuvenation and pollution abatement programmes. Recognising the importance of rivers as vital sources of irrigation, drinking 122 122 water, biodiversity and cultural heritage, the Water Resources Department is implementing comprehensive initiatives for the rejuvenation of the Cauvery, Vaigai and Tamirabarani rivers. The Department is coordinating with various stakeholder departments and local bodies to prevent the discharge of untreated sewage and industrial effluents into rivers through the establishment of adequate sewage treatment infrastructure, impro ved solid waste management systems and effective environmental monitoring. Simultaneously, riverfront development, biodiversity conservation, afforestation, river surface cleaning and public awareness programmes are being integrated into river restoration initiatives to ensure sustainable management of river ecosystems. Under the Nadanthaai Vaazhi Cauvery Project, comprehensive interventions have been proposed for pollution abatement, sewage management, riverfront development, biodiversity enhancement, soli d waste 123 123 management and conservation of the historic Grand Anicut (Kallanai) region.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: Under the Nadanthaai Vaazhi Cauvery Project, comprehensive interventions have been proposed for pollution abatement, sewage management, riverfront development, biodiversity enhancement, soli d waste 123 123 management and conservation of the historic Grand Anicut (Kallanai) region. Similar integrated river rejuvenation programmes are being taken up for the Vaigai and Tamirabarani rivers with emphasis on improving water quality, preventing pollution, r estoring ecological habitats and creating environmentally sustainable public spaces along river corridors. The Clean Rivers initiative also supports continuous monitoring of water quality, prevention of illegal waste disposal, strengthening of institutiona l coordination and promotion of community participation in river conservation. These initiatives will contribute towards restoring river ecosystems, improving environmental quality, protecting aquatic biodiversity and ensuring safe and sustainable water resources for future generations. Rivers Conservation Project In the year 2026 -27, this Government have allocated an amount of Rs.25 crore to conduct comprehensive detailed studies and prepare 124 124 Detailed Project Reports for the Projects for rejuvenation of Cau very, Vaigai and Thamirabarani. a. Nadanthaai Vaazhi Cauvery Project The prime objective of Nadanthaai Vaazhi Cauvery Project is to rejuvenate and to effectively curb sewage polluting the Cauvery River and its tributaries in Tamil Nadu. The preliminary Proje ct Report for an amount of Rs.11,250 crore was sent to Ministry of Jal Shakti, Central Government for in-principle approval on 21.10.2019 and Central Government communicated its observations on 10.02.2020.

items.text: The preliminary Proje ct Report for an amount of Rs.11,250 crore was sent to Ministry of Jal Shakti, Central Government for in-principle approval on 21.10.2019 and Central Government communicated its observations on 10.02.2020. The project has been planned for implementation i n two phases and the preparation of Detailed Project Report has been entrusted to WAPCOS Limited. Based on the advice of the National River Conservation Directorate, the Detailed Project Report for the first phase has been prepared and technical clearance obtained from the 125 125 Environment Protection Training and Research Institute, Hyderabad. In continuation of above, the National River Conservation Directorate has approved a cost of Rs.934.301 crore as follows: Sl. No. Work Components Estimate Amount (Rs. in Crore) 1 Sewage Management 577.151 2 Riverfront Development Activities 176.98 3 River Surface Cleaning 27.00 4 Solid Waste Management 30.89 5 Cauvery Village - People Participation and creating awareness 6.00 6 Online monitoring 27.58 7 Kallanai Museum 36.70 8 Biodiversity Conservation 52.00 Total 934.301 126 126 The funding pattern of Central and the State Government is 60:40. The Central Government share is Rs.560.581 Crore and the State Government share is Rs.373.720 Crore. Apart from this, the Central Government has requested the State Government to bear Rs.377.979 Crore for Operation & Maintenance, Labour Welfare Fund and Rehabilitation and Resettlement works. Proposals for submitting revised Detailed Project Report (DPR) incorporating the replies on observation of the Central Government and acceptance for State share and Operation and Maintenance cost are under consideration of the Government. b.

items.text: Proposals for submitting revised Detailed Project Report (DPR) incorporating the replies on observation of the Central Government and acceptance for State share and Operation and Maintenance cost are under consideration of the Government. b. Tamirabarani River Rejuvenation Project The Government of Tamil Nadu has accorded high priority to the rejuve nation and sustainable management of the Tamirabarani river, the only perennial river of the State, with the objective of restoring its ecological integrity, 127 127 improving water quality, enhancing groundwater recharge and ensuring the long -term sustainability of its water resources. The Tamirabarani River Rejuvenation Project, at an estimated cost of Rs.1,134.10 crore, has been formulated adopting an integrated river basin management approach encompassing pollution abatement, river conservation, ecological restoration and community participation. The project envisages a comprehensive package of interventions, including prevention of solid waste dumping through fencing, riverfront development, construction and modernisation of bathing ghats and public amenities, river surface cleaning, biodiversity conservation and afforestation, construction of groundwater recharge structures and Barrages, rehabilitation of existing Anicuts and Channels, rehabilitation and resettlement in high -risk flood-prone areas, survey and d emarcation of river boundaries and establishment of an online real -time monitoring system for sewage and industrial effluent discharge. The project also promotes community 128 128 participation through “Porunai Gramam” and awareness programmes for sustainable rive r conservation.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The project also promotes community 128 128 participation through “Porunai Gramam” and awareness programmes for sustainable rive r conservation. The project is expected to significantly improve river water quality, restore the ecological integrity of the Tamirabarani river, augment groundwater resources, strengthen flood resilience, prevent encroachments and pollution, enhance biodi versity and create improved public amenities along the river corridor. The integrated interventions will contribute to sustainable water resources management, improved environmental conditions and enhanced livelihood opportunities for the people dependent on the Tamirabarani river basin. c. Vaigai River Rejuvenation Project The Government of Tamil Nadu has accorded high priority to the rejuvenation of the Vaigai river with the objective of restoring its ecological integrity, improving water quality, strengthening irrigation infrastructure and 129 129 ensuring sustainable management of water resources in the Vaigai Basin. The Vaigai river Rejuvenation Project, at an estimated cost of Rs.917.40 crore, has been formulated adopting an integrated river restoration approach covering the polluted stretches of the river in Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Sivagangai and Ramanathapuram Districts. The project aims to address river pollution, augment groundwater resources, improve river ecology and enhance the environmental and socio -economic benefits derived from the river system. The Vaigai river originates in the Western Ghats and traverses about 258 km before joining the Palk Bay, draining an area of approximately 7,150 sq. km across ten sub - basins.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Vaigai river originates in the Western Ghats and traverses about 258 km before joining the Palk Bay, draining an area of approximately 7,150 sq. km across ten sub - basins. Over the years, increasing urbanisa tion, discharge of untreated sewage, indiscriminate disposal of solid waste, encroachments and degradation of Riverine ecosystems have adversely affected the health of the river. The project therefore envisages a comprehensive package of interventions, 130 130 including sewage interception, diversion and treatment through sewage treatment plants, solid waste management, desilting, bio - remediation, afforestation, construction and modernisation of Checkdams, Bed dams and Regulators, flood protection works, river regrading, removal of invasive Prosopis juliflora (Seemai Karuvelam), development of bathing ghats, parks and riverfront amenities, aesthetic lighting, recharge wells and other groundwater recharge structures. The project is expected to significantly improve river water quality, restore aquatic biodiversity, enhance dissolved oxygen levels and strengthen groundwater recharge across the basin. The proposed interventions will also improve irrigation infrastructure benefiting about 2.25 lakh acre of ayacut, enhance drinking water security, strengthen flood resilience, improve public amenities along the river corridor and promote sustainable environmental management. 131 131 The project will facilitate long -term conservation of the river through boundary demarcation, geot agging of river assets and integrated river basin management, thereby ensuring the ecological restoration and sustainable development of the Vaigai river for the benefit of present and future generations. ii.

River Linking Projects The river - linking projects connecting Cauvery – Vaigai - Gundar, South Pennar - Palar, Pennar - Cheyyar, and Tamirabarani - Vaippar have been announced but are yet to be fully implemented. To expedite the execution, Rs.5,OOO crore will be allocated and the works will be completed s oon (Vetri Thamizhagam Vision). Tamil Nadu is characterised by highly uneven spatial and temporal distribution of rainfall. While certain river basins receive substantial flood flows during the monsoon, many other regions experience recurring droughts and water scarcity. The interlinking of 132 132 rivers has therefore been identified as one of the most effective long-term strategies for equitable distribution of water resources across the State. The primary objective of river linking is to harness surplus floodwat ers that would otherwise flow into the sea and divert them to water-deficit regions through scientifically designed canal systems. Such inter -basin diversion not only improves irrigation facilities but also contributes significantly towards groundwater rec harge, stabilisation of existing ayacut, enhancement of tank storage, mitigation of flood damages and improvement of drinking water security. Accordingly, this Government is formulating and implementing several major river linking projects.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]

items.text: Accordingly, this Government is formulating and implementing several major river linking projects. These include t he Cauvery (Kattalai) – Vaigai - Gundar Link, Pennaiyar - Cheyyar Link, Pennaiyar (Nedungal Anicut) - Palar Link and Tamirabarani – Kallar - Vaippar Link. These projects are at various stages such as land acquisition, detailed project report preparation, technical appraisal and execution. 133 133 On completion, these projects are expected to substantially increase irrigation potential, improve water availability in drought -prone districts, rejuvenate tanks and reservoirs, strengthen groundwater resources and provid e long-term socio -economic benefits to farming communities. Under the Vetri Thamizhagam Vision, th is Government will continue to accord high priority to expedite these strategic projects through phased implementation based on technical feasibility, environ mental sustainability and availability of financial resources. This programme will include major projects such as: Anaimalaiyaru - Nallar Link Project (Tiruppur / Coimbatore) E rdhalavu - Pulikkarai Link Project (Dharmapuri) Construction of check dams and regulators in the Cauvery and Thirumanimutharu regions of Namakkal district Upper Vaippar and Mudangiyar river restoration project (Virudhunagar / Rajapalayam) Ramanathi - Jambu r iver link canal project (Tenkasi / Alangulam) Tamirabarani – Karumeniyar - Nambiyar river link project (Tirunelveli / Thoothukudi) along with several other important schemes (Vetri Thamizhagam Vision).

items.text: The Government of Tamil Nadu has accorded high priorit y to the timely implementation of major and medium irrigation projects under a Mission Mode Programme to accelerate the creation of irrigation infrastructure, improve water use efficiency and enhance agricultural productivity. The Water 144 144 Resources Departmen t has identified several strategically important projects that have the potential to augment irrigation, utilise surplus floodwaters, restore river systems and strengthen climate resilience in water -deficit regions of the State. Under this initiative, th is Government is formulating and implementing projects such as the Tamirabarani – Karumeniyar – Nambiyar Link, Jerthalav – Pulikkarai Link, Ramanadhi – Jambunadhi Link Canal, Barrages across the Cauvery Basin, Flood Water Diversion to Thirumanimuthar Sub basin, Upper Vaippar and Mudangiyar Restoration and the Anaimalaiyar – Nallar Link. These projects are at various stages of completion, detailed project report preparation, technical appraisal and administrative approval. The completed Tamirabarani – Karumeniyar – Nambiyar River Linking Project has demonstrated the benefits of integrated water resources planning by facilitating the transfer of surplus floodwaters to water -deficit regions, 145 145 thereby improving irrigation, groundwater recharge and water availabilit y in the southern districts. Building upon this success, the Department proposes additional interventions to strengthen the project and improve the performance of the irrigation system.

items.text: Building upon this success, the Department proposes additional interventions to strengthen the project and improve the performance of the irrigation system. The Jerthalav – Pulikkarai Link Project is under implementation to div ert surplus water of the Chinnar River to drought -prone Tanks in Dharmapuri District, while the Ramanadhi – Jambunadhi Link Canal is nearing completion and will improve irrigation facilities by supplying surplus floodwaters to the Jambunadhi system tanks i n Tenkasi District. Simultaneously, proposals for constructing new Barrages across the Cauvery and Kollidam rivers and for lifting surplus floodwaters to the Thirumanimuthar Sub basin are being pursued to enhance water conservation, strengthen groundwater recharge and mitigate flood damages. 146 146 To ensure groundwater recharge, availability of fresh water for irrigation and conservation of water during the monsoon, this Government has allocated Rs.10 crore for detailed feasibility study and report for the construction of Barrages across the River Cauvery. This Government is also formulating restoration programmes for the Upper Vaippar and Mudangiyar river systems through desilting, river training, strengthening of riverbanks and rehabilitation of damaged hydraulic structures. These interventions will improve conveyance efficiency, restore river integrity and ensure sustainable irrigation for extensive ayacut areas. Under the Vetri Thamizhagam Vision, th is Government will continue to accord high priority to expedit e these Mission Mode projects to create resilient irrigation infrastructure capable of addressing future water challenges while ensuring equitable distribution of water 147 147 resources, improved agricultural production and enhanced livelihood opportunities for f arming communities across Tamil Nadu. 148 148 5. items.text: 148 148 5. Dams i. State Dam Safety Organization The key function of State Dam Safety Organisation (SDSO) is to provide perpetual surveillance, regular safety inspections and monitoring of 123 specified Dams located within the State. The State Project Management Unit under this Wing is the Nodal Agency for implementation of Dam Rehabilitation and Improvement Project. In this Project Rehabilitation works in Dams are being carried out, under World Bank assistance. The Dam Safety Act, 2021, notified by the Central Government on 14.12.2021, came into force with effect from 30.12.2021, vide notification dated 28.12.2021. To implement the Dam Safety Act, 2021 in the State, t he Government of Tamil Nadu have issued notification for the Constitution of State Committee on Dam Safety (SCDS) and State Dam Safety Organisation (SDSO) vide G.O. (Ms) 149 149 No.56, Water Resources (WR -2) Department dated 30.06.2022. State Committee on Dam Safety (SCDS) State Committee on Dam Safety (SCDS) has been cons tituted as per Dam Safety Act, 2021. This Committee shall meet twice in a year and one meeting shall be held before the onset of monsoon. The Committee has to be reconstituted for every three years thereafter. Recently, the Committee has been reconstituted and notified. So far, six meetings of State Committee on Dam Safety (SCDS) have been conducted at Chennai. The activities of the State Dam Safety Organisation are reviewed by the State Committee on Dam Safety.

Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies under Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of water bodies is being implemented under Pradhan Mantri Krishi S inchayee Yojana – Har Khet Ko Pani (PMKSY -HKKP). Formation of New Drinking Water Reservoir in Kovalam Sub Basin (Mamallan Reservoir) To augment drinking water supply to Chennai and its suburban areas and to decentralise the existing water supply system, the formation of a new drinking water Reservoir, namely Mamallan Reservoir, in the Kovalam Sub Basin between the East Coast Road (ECR) and Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) in Thiruporur and Thirukalukundram Taluks of Chengalpattu District, with a storage capacity of 1.65 TMC is in progress. The estimated cost of this project is Rs.342.60 crore. This Reservoir is being formed in about 5,161 acre of Government land and is designed to harness surplus monsoon runoff f rom the catchment comprising 69 Tanks and lakes in the region. Annual yield at 75% dependability has been assessed as 2.97 TMC, of which 1.65 TMC will be stored for drinking water purposes, while 182 182 the balance flow will be released to the Muttukadu and Kokki lamedu estuaries to maintain ecological requirements. So far, 10% of the works have been completed and the remaining works are under progress. 183 183 9.

items.text: So far, 10% of the works have been completed and the remaining works are under progress. 183 183 9. Climate Change and Disaster Management i. Cauvery Delta Ecological Restoration Mission The Cauvery Delta region is the heart of Tamil Nadu’s agriculture. However, environmental degradation has severely affected its water resources, soil fertility, and agricultural productivity. To restore the Cauvery Delta, an allocation of Rs.5,OOO crore will be made, with special focus on addressing groundwater salinity in the Cauvery Delta. Additional measures will also be undertaken to improve depleted groundwater levels and restore soil fertility (Vetri Thamizhagam Vision). The Cauvery Delta is one of the most productive agricu ltural regions in the country and serves as the principal food grain producing area of Tamil Nadu. However, the Delta has been experiencing increasing challenges arising from declining groundwater levels, saline water intrusion, deterioration of irrigation infrastructure, climate variability and reduced 184 184 river flows. Recognising these challenges, the Government will launch a comprehensive “Cauvery Delta Ecological Restoration Mission” to ensure the long -term sustainability of the Delta ecosystem. The Mission adopts an integrated approach towards restoring the hydrological and ecological health of the Delta through a combination of structural and non -structural interventions. Priority is being accorded to the construction of tail-end Regulators, Cross Regulato rs, Intermediate Regulators, Check structures and Groundwater recharge measures to prevent saline water intrusion, improve freshwater retention and enhance groundwater availability. The Department is implementing the Climate Adaptation in Vennar Sub -Basin Project, which aims to improve irrigation efficiency, reduce groundwater salinity and strengthen climate resilience in vulnerable areas of the Delta.
items.source: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27 [Water Resources department]
items.title: Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department: Policy Note 2026-27

items.text: The Department is implementing the Climate Adaptation in Vennar Sub -Basin Project, which aims to improve irrigation efficiency, reduce groundwater salinity and strengthen climate resilience in vulnerable areas of the Delta. Simultaneously, proposals have been formulated for the creation of freshwater storage facilities, includin g the formation of a 185 185 freshwater tank at Karapidagai Village in Nagapattinam District by converting an existing saline water body into a sustainable drinking water source. In addition, the Department is preparing comprehensive proposals for the rehabilitati on and modernisation of irrigation infrastructure in the Kollidam Basin through restoration of damaged Regulators, Sluices, Checkdams, Escapes and Canal systems. These interventions are expected to improve irrigation management, enhance groundwater recharg e, prevent seawater intrusion and restore the ecological balance of the Cauvery Delta. The Mission will significantly contribute towards sustaining agricultural productivity, improving water availability, enhancing groundwater quality and ensuring long -term environmental security for the Cauvery Delta region. An amount of Rs.10 crore has been allocated during 2026 -27 for feasibility study 186 186 and project report for Ecological Restoration of the Cauvery Delta region. ii. Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience Project in Cauvery Delta In this project, construction of additional tail end Regulators, reconstruction and rehabilitation of Regulators, desilting and widening of drains to appropriate standards are being taken up. Under Phase-II of the project, it is proposed to take up Vennar, Paminiyar, Koraiyar, Kaduvaiyar, Maraikkakoraiyar and Manankondanar and 6 pumping schemes at a cost of Rs.1,825.00 crore. iii.

items.text: Greater Chennai Water Supply Augmentation and Flood Mitigation Resilient to Climate Change It is very imperative to protect Greater Chennai from recurrent flooding and drinking water problems. Short-term and Long-term flood mitigation works are proposed to be taken up to avoid recurring flooding in Greater Chennai. 187 187 At present, five Reservoirs viz., Cholavaram, Chem barambakkam, Poondi, Redhills, Kannankottai - Thervaikandigai and Veeranam Tank with a combined capacity of 13.222 TMC cater to the needs of drinking water requirements of Greater Chennai as against the annual demand of drinking and industrial requirement about 22 TMC at present and which may raise to 32 TMC by 2035 with the projected population growth. In the recent past, serious impact of Climate Change has been observed on tropical climatic areas causing unprecedented flash floods in many parts of Chennai, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur Districts. Hence, with an aim to bridge the gap between present water demand and supply rate and also to create a flood resilient urban Infrastructure, the project “Greater Chennai Water Supply Augmentation a nd Flood Mitigation Resilient to Climate Change” is being formulated. 188 188 The objective of the proposal is flood mitigation and rainwater conservation for deficit years in and around Greater Chennai. The Comprehensive proposal comprises enhancing the rain wate r storage capacity in the upstream of Greater Chennai by creation of new storage structures, increasing the storage capacity of existing water bodies, improving the conveyance efficiency and interconnecting the feasible water bodies.

items.text: The Comprehensive proposal comprises enhancing the rain wate r storage capacity in the upstream of Greater Chennai by creation of new storage structures, increasing the storage capacity of existing water bodies, improving the conveyance efficiency and interconnecting the feasible water bodies. The proposal aims to c reate an additional storage capacity of 20.50 TMC to meet the drinking water requirements of Greater Chennai and to find permanent mitigation measures to a maximum extent for the flood vulnerable areas in and around Greater Chennai. This scheme has been fo rmulated at an estimated cost of Rs.22,004 crore tentatively. This Government has allocated an amount of Rs.42 crore for 202 pre -monsoon preparedness works in Chennai, Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu and Cuddalore Districts for the year 2026-27. 189 189 10. Desilting and Sand Mining i. Free Issue of Vandal The storage capacity of water bodies in Tamil Nadu has declined over time due to siltation. As the deposited silt is rich in micro - nutrients and serves as an effective organic manure, the Government permits f armers to remove it free of cost, thereby restoring the storage capacity of tanks while improving soil fertility and agricultural productivity. Clay, silt, savudu and gravel from tank beds, channels and reservoirs may be removed free of cost by farmers, po ttery workers and the local public for agricultural, domestic and pottery purposes, with permission from the competent authority after due notification. The permissible quantity is 75 cubic metres per acre for wetlands, 90 cubic metres per acre for dry lan ds (once in two years), 30 cubic metres for domestic use, and 60 cubic metres for pottery purposes.

items.text: The permissible quantity is 75 cubic metres per acre for wetlands, 90 cubic metres per acre for dry lan ds (once in two years), 30 cubic metres for domestic use, and 60 cubic metres for pottery purposes. 190 190 To facilitate timely desilting before the monsoon, the Government, through G.O. (Ms) No.14, Natural Resources (MMC -1) Department, dated 12.06.2024, amended the Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1959, simplifying the procedure by delegating approval powers from District Collectors to Tahsildars, prescribing a 30 -day period for removal of silt and clay, and enabling faster processing of farmers' applications. Further, the entire process —from application to verification and grant of permission—has been made online, ensuring transparent and speedy approvals. This initiative promotes effective desilting of water bodies, enhances their storage capacity, imp roves soil fertility, and supports sustainable agricultural productivity across the State. The Hon’ble Chief Minister ordered on 20.05.2026 that the District Collectors should expedite this scheme and publish the list of tanks for the year 2026-2027 in the district-level gazette and monitor the scheme as per the rules and guidelines. 191 191 ii. items.text: The scheme is being implemented with a funding pattern of 60:40 between the Central and State Governments. Under the programme, the Palladam Extension Canal Cluster in Tiruppur District, covering a Cultivable Command Area (CCA) of 4,991 Ha. and benefiting 11 Villages, has been approved for implementation under Phase -I of the scheme. The app roved project cost is Rs.99.03 crore. 194 194 The Government of India has appointed an empanelled consultant for preparation of the Detailed Design Report (DDR) for the project. Based on the detailed investigations and design studies, the DDR has been prepared for an estimated cost of Rs.131.79 crore. As envisaged in the scheme guidelines, the District Level Implementation Committee (DLIC), State Level Steering Committee (SLSC), and State Project Management Unit (SPMU) have been constituted for effective implementation, monitoring and stakeholder participation. The Irrigation Management Training Institute, Tiruchira ppalli is designated to act as Farmer Relationship Agency (FRA) for this project. The proposal for according Administrative Sanction to this project is under consideration. 195 195 12. Activities of Functional Wings i. Plan Formulation This wing plays a very crucial role in the development and augmentation of water resources in the State. It undertakes studies and preparation of Preliminary Feasibility Reports for all types of Major, Medium and Minor irrigation schemes and River interlinking schemes, preparation of Detailed Project Reports for technical and economic feasibility projects and onward submission to the Government.

items.text: It undertakes studies and preparation of Preliminary Feasibility Reports for all types of Major, Medium and Minor irrigation schemes and River interlinking schemes, preparation of Detailed Project Reports for technical and economic feasibility projects and onward submission to the Government. Being, the Nodal Agency for Water Resou rces Department Budget Announcements Schemes, it scrutinizes the estimates of Announcement works received from all the offices of Water Resources Department across the state and forwards them to Government for Administrative sanction. The Environmental re lated activities are carried out by this wing through three Environmental Cell Divisions functioning under the Plan Formulation Circle, Salem. 196 196 This wing also acts as a Nodal Agency for obtaining funds under NABARD Financial assistance and Pradhan Mantri Kr ishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) schemes. ii. Design Research and Construction Support This wing acts as a nodal agency for Repair, Renovation and Restoration of water bodies, Desilting of Reservoirs in the State and Coastal Protection Works under Integrated Co astal Zone Management Project. The Designs Circle functioning under this wing evolves design and drawings for irrigation structures such as reservoir, canal, tank, anicut, regulator and check dam. This Circle also recommends necessary remedial measures for the problems such as cracks, seepage and leakage that occur in the irrigation structures. The Soil Mechanics & Research Division acting as the Central Quality Control Laboratory at Chennai conducts tests for finding soil 197 197 characteristics and quality checki ng tests for concrete and construction materials. The Institute of Hydraulics and Hydrology established in the year 1944 at Poondi, consists of Hydraulics Division at Poondi and Watershed Management Board Division (WSMB) at Pollachi.

items.text: The Institute of Hydraulics and Hydrology established in the year 1944 at Poondi, consists of Hydraulics Division at Poondi and Watershed Management Board Division (WSMB) at Pollachi. The Hydraulics Divisi on is engaged in carrying out basic research and conducting model studies in the field of hydraulics, hydrology and irrigation. Research on coastal engineering, monitoring through collecting data and conducting research on shoreline oscillation phenomena at certain selected points along the eastern and western coast of Tamil Nadu are carried out. The WSMB Division is entrusted in undertaking sedimentation and watershed management studies in Reservoirs and Tanks across Tamil Nadu. In addition, capacity loss in Reservoirs due to siltation is calculated and remedial measures to reduce the entry of sediments into Reservoirs from the watershed areas are suggested by this premier institution. 198 198 iii. Operation & Maintenance This wing scrutinizes the estimates received from the Regional Chief Engineers for Hydro Mechanical components, shutters and its components in Dams, Sluices and Weirs for obtaining approval from the Government. This wing is also entrusted with the preparation of Standard Data and Standard Schedule of Ra tes (SoR) for Hydro -Mechanical works for adoption in the preparation of estimates. The status reports of elections for Water Users Associations, Distributary Committees and Project Committees under Water Resources Consolidation Project (WRCP) are consolida ted and sent to the Government from this Wing. The Public Works Workshop & Stores Division under this wing procures new vehicles, condemns old vehicles, unserviceable machineries and obsolete spares of various machineries. This Division also undertakes inspection and issuance of stability certificates to amusement rides in Government permitted 199 199 exhibitions.

Advocating Judicious use of Water The State Ground and Surface Water Resources Data Centre has a monitoring network of 3,414 open wells and 1,700 piezometers. The water level is being monitored every month and a district wise average water level comparison report is being prepared and uploaded in the website www.groundwatertnpwd.org.in. Tamil Nadu Water Resources Conservation and River Restoration Corporation (TNWRCRRC) The Tamil Nadu Water Resources Conservation and Rivers Restoration Corporation has been registered with the Registrar of Companies, Chennai and incorporated with effect from 25.12.2019. Th e main objective of the Corporation is to promote water conservation, reclamation of Tanks, Rivers and modernize the existing irrigation infrastructures. The Corporation will also focus on interconnecting flood surplus Canals and interlinking of Rivers and River basins. Promotion of climate resilient infrastructure with special emphasis on prevention of sea water intrusion, wet land conservation and flood 210 210 mitigation will be the other priority areas for the Corporation. International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage(ICID) The International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage (ICID), established in 1950 and headquartered in New Delhi, is a global non-profit organization that promotes efficient irrigation, drainage, flood management and agricultural water management. To recognize excellence in irrigation, drainage and sustainable agricultural water management worldwide, the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage (ICID) has been conferring prestigious recognitions such as the World Heritage Irrigation Structure (WHIS) Award to historically significant and well- functioning irrigation systems. Over the years, these awards have highlighted remarkable contributions in preserving traditional water systems and promoting sustainable water management practices across the globe.

items.text: Over the years, these awards have highlighted remarkable contributions in preserving traditional water systems and promoting sustainable water management practices across the globe. 213 213 The ICID announced the conferment of the WHIS Awards for the year 2025, recognizing outstanding heritage irrigat ion structures of global importance. In 2025, ICID recognized Tamil Nadu’s historical water management excellence by awarding the prestigious World Heritage Irrigation Structure (WHIS) Award to three remarkable systems: • Cheyyar Anicut – An ancient diversio n structure showcasing early engineering skill in River water management. • Kodiveri Anicut and Channel System – Built across the Bhavani River, known for its stone masonry and efficient canal system. • Noyyal River System Tanks – A traditional interconnected tank system designed for water storage, distribution, and groundwater recharge. This recognition highlights Tamil Nadu’s long-standing expertise in sustainable irrigation and community -based water management 214 214 systems that are not only historically significa nt but still relevant in addressing modern water challenges. ii. Spring Census Achievement The Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, is the apex national authority responsible for policy formulation, planning and implementation of programmes related to water resources management, including drinking water, irrigation, groundwater development and river rejuvenation across the country. To strengthen scientific understanding and sustainable management of natural water sources, the Ministry has initiated the First Digital Spring Census / Spring Water Survey Programme, aimed at the systematic identification, geo -tagging, mapping and scientific assessment of natural springs, including evaluation of discharge, seasonal variability, water quality and recharge characteristics, particularly in hilly and groundwater-stressed regions.

items.text: 5.6 Finance Tamil Nadu Power Generation Corporation Limited plays a significant role in meeting the power generation requirements of Tamil Nadu 38 38 and ensuring uninterrupted power supply across the State. In order to strengthen the financial position of TNPGCL and support its operational and infrastructure requirements, the Government of Tamil Nadu has been continuously extending financial assistance through Government Guarantees for loans availed by the Corporation. These guarantees enable TNPGCL to mobilize funds fro m financial institutions at competitive interest rates for meeting its capital expenditure and operational commitments. During the financial year 2025 –26, the Government has provided Government Guarantees amounting to ₹ 19,986.56 crore in favour of TNPGCL. The continued support of the Government reflects its commitment towards improving the financial sustainability and operational efficiency of TNPGCL. 39 The actual expenditure incurred by TNPGCL has exceeded the expenditure approved by the Hon’ble Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission under the Tariff Order, which has resulted in further financial stress on the Corporation. Following the demerger of the company, a Mid- Term Review Petition for financial year 2024 –25 has been filed before Hon’ble TNERC seeking approval for additional revenue requirements. Upon approval of the petition, TNPGCL is expected to realize additional revenue, which would help in reducing the losses to a considerable extent. In order to improve the operational and financial performance of the Corporation, several cost-control measures and revenue augmentation initiatives are being undertaken. Continuous efforts are being made to operate the power plants at maximum efficiency levels to enhance generation and improve revenue 39 38 and ensuring uninterrupted power supply across the State.

Further, it aims to achieve a 70% reduction in carbon emissions by 2031 through the implementation of comprehensive clean energy initiatives, 43 enhanced energy efficiency measures and the promotion of low -carbon technologies. The key objectives and functions of TNGECL include:  Increasing the share of renewable energy in the State's total energy consumption to 50 percent by 2031. 44 44  Promoting large-scale solar and wind power projects across the State.  Encouraging the installation of rooftop solar photovoltaic systems in residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional sectors.  Supporting the generation of energy from renewable resources, including bio -energy and other non-conventional energy sources.  Formulating and implementing a Renewable Energy Hybrid Policy to enhance renewable energy integration and improve grid reliability.  Optimizing the utilization of existing transmission and distribution infrastructure based on technical feasibility and system efficiency. 45  Facilitating access to affordable and sustainable financing for renewable energy and green infrastructure projects. Through these strategic initiatives, Tamil Nadu aims to strengthen its leadership in renewable energy, enhance energy security, promote sustainable economic development, create green employment opportunities and contribute significantly to India's climate commitments and the achievement of long- term net-zero objectives. 6.2 Wind Power With an installed wind energy capacity of 11,686.21 MW (including Central Transmission Utility) as on 01.07.2026, the State ranks second in the country in terms of installed wind power capacity.

items.text: The State generates about 16,600 million units of wind energy annually, contributing nearly 12% of its total electricity 46 46 consumption and playing a vital role in strengthening its clean energy portfolio. The State possesses an estimated onshore wind energy potential of approximately 95 GW at a height of 150 metres , providing significant scope for further expansion of wind power generation. The Muppandal Wind Farm, located in Tamil Nadu, is one of the world's largest operational onshore wind farms and stands as a landmark in India's renewable energy journey. It exemplifies the State's long -standing commitment to the development and large -scale deployment of wind energy technologies. Going forward, the Government promote s the addition of new wind capacity, repowering of ageing wind turbines, modernization of grid infrastructure and integration of advanced forecasting and scheduling mechanisms to 47 maximize renewable energy generation and improve grid reliability. 6.2.1 Initiatives to Streamline Wind Power Sector TNGECL (erstwhile TANGEDCO), under the Tirunelveli NCES Circle, owns four wind farm sites at Kayathar-I, Kayathar-II, Muppandal, and Puliyankulam with 110 WEGs having a total installed capacity of 17.355 MW. The Government has proposed to replace the above ageing wind turbines to repower the sites with 1 8.75 MW of wind capacity and a 16 MW solar plant as a Hybrid Project. Tender is under process for executing the above scheme. 6.3 Solar Power Solar power complements the State's substantial wind energy capacity, contributing significantly to meet the growing demand for clean and sustainable energy.

The scheme envisages saturation of rooftop solar installations on all technic ally feasible Government buildings and encourages States to undertake similar initiatives. In line with this objective and to strengthen energy security while advancing the State’s renewable energy goals, the Government of Tamil Nadu proposed to utilize vacant rooftop spaces in Government buildings under the Renewable Energy Service Company (RESCO) Model. TNGECL has been designated as the nodal agency for implementation of the 57 programme and is responsible for tendering, project management, monitoring and coordination with all stakeholders. Under the RESCO model, the selected developer will undertake the design, supply, installation, commissioning, operation and maintenance of rooftop solar plants for a period of 25 years. A tender has been floated for the selection of developers for establishing 20 MW of grid-connected rooftop solar projects on Government buildings in Chennai, Chengalpattu, Kanchipuram and Tiruvallur districts. The construction of 3 Nos weirs completed. Other civil, mechanical, and electrical works are in progress. The project has achieved 94.25% physical progress and 93.57% financial progress 68 68 till date. The project is expected to be commissioned in June 2027. 6.7.3.2 Kundah Pumped Storage Hydro Electric Project (4x125 MW) Kundah Pumped Storage Hydro Electric Project (4x125 MW) is being developed in the Nilgiris district at a cost of ₹3,926.80 crore. The 'Porthimund' and 'Avalanche -Emerald' reservoirs owned by the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Ltd., will be used as the 'Upper' and 'Lower' reservoirs respectively for this project. During times of low power demand, surplus power will be utilised for pumping water through the Plant under construction from the Avalanche - Emerald reservoirs to the Porthimund reservoir. The same water will be used for power generation during peak hour demand.

TAMILNADU TRANSMISSION CORPORATION LIMITED Introduction Tamil Nadu’s transmission network serves as the backbone of its power sector, ensuring that electricity generated from thermal, hydro, and renewable sources, seamlessly reaches households, industries, and essential services across the State. Structurally, it comprises a robust, layered grid of Extra High Voltage (EHV) substations and transmission lines which transmit power throughout Tamil Nadu and steps down voltage safely and efficiently for regional distribution. The grid interconnects these transmission lines into a unified system, balancing sup ply and demand, providing alternate routes during network faults and facilitate the large -scale integration of green energy . Together, the 75 transmission network and grid act as the electric highway, delivering reliable, stable and uninterrupted power across the State.

Supported by three Sub -LDCs at Chennai, Erode and Madurai, it ensures efficient grid control and coordination.

items.text: Supported by three Sub -LDCs at Chennai, Erode and Madurai, it ensures efficient grid control and coordination. Its primary functions include maintaining grid parameters within the limits prescribed by the Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC), such as frequency between 49.90 and 50.05 Hz and drawal deviations within ±250 MW. SLDC plays a balancing role by matching load with available generation in real time, supervising grid operations and exercising control over the intra-state transmission system to guarantee reliability and stability. TN grid experiences five distinct demand peaks, namely, morning peak, solar peak, evening peak, lighting peak and AC night peak. At present, the solar and evening peaks are 97 largely met through renewable energy sources such as wind and solar, supplemented by other generators. However, shortages are often encountered during the morning, lighting, and AC peaks, particularly in the months of February to May. After meeting the demand with available sources viz., thermal, hydro, IPP, CPP, Co -gen, Biomass, Central Generating Stations (CGS) share, Long term open Access (LTOA), Medium term open Access (MTOA) and renewable energy sources, the shortage in demand is met through short term tie ups such as Day Ahead Market (DAM), Day Ahead Contingency (DAC) Market, Long duration contract (LDC) and Real Time Market (RTM). All critical feeders are monitored and decisions taken to avoid overloading due to tripping of feeders. Emergency Line clears are decided and given in the real time to minimise the interruptions.

items.text: With the increasing share of renewable energy (RE), 112 112 which is seasonal and intermittent in nature, it has become essential to accurately assess the demand–supply balance in the grid. To facilitate the Resource Ad equacy exercise, Purchase Orders have been placed for the procurement of software tool. The software is being designed to generate robust demand projections by considering historical consumption patterns, sector -wise demand growth, weather parameters, economic parameters, Government policies, energy efficiency measures and emerging demand drivers such as electric vehicles, data centers, green hydrogen and roof top solar installations in compliance with the provisions of the TNERC Resource Adequacy Regulations 2025. The study considers conventional and renewable energy sources, energy storage systems, power procurement options, retirement of ageing generating stations and operational 113 constraints to determine the optimal least- cost resource mix. The outcome of the study will provide a scientific and data -driven basis for long- term power procurement planning, generation capacity augmentation and investment decisions enabling TNPDCL to ensure a reliable and uninterrupted power supply to the consumers. items.text: India is committed to achieving the SDGs through various national programmes and policies, with NITI Aayog coordinating and monitoring progress across the country. Tamil Nadu has aligned its development initiatives with the SDGs by focusing on sustainable energy, climate action, healthcare, education, social welfare and economic growth. Through outcome based planning and effective implementation, Tamil Nadu continues to 137 contribute towards achieving sustainable and inclusive development. Goal 7 , which pertains to TNEB Limited , aims to “Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all.” The other related goals are Goal 1, Goal 8, Goal 9, Goal 12, and Goal 13. For Goal 7, the associated Working Group is “Working Group 5 – Innovation, Industrialization and Sustainable Development”, and the Nodal Department is the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department. The key targets under Goal 7 are: • 7.1: Ensuring access to affordable, reliable, and modern energy services. • 7.2: Substantially increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix. • 7.3: Doubling the global rate of improvement in energy efficiency. 137 136 • Testing of BEE Star Labelled Appliances and Market Surveillance activities • Establishment of Energy Clubs 8.15 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a set of 17 global goals adopted by the United Nations in 2015 under the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development to achieve a better and more sustainable future for all. items.text: 160 160 10. TAMIL NADU ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION Introduction The Government of Tamil Nadu constituted the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) vide G.O.Ms.No.58, Energy (A1) Department, dated 17th March 1999 in accordance with section 1 7(1) of the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998 (Central Act, 14 of 1998), which has since been repealed by section 185(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (Central Act, 36 of 2003). However, the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission established under the said repealed Central Act, 14 of 1998 continues to be the State Electricity Regulatory Commission by virtue of the first proviso to sub -section (1) of section 82 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (Central Act, 36 of 2003). The Commission is empow ered to make Regulations for the conduct of its proceedings 161 and discharge of its functions. As per section 95 of Electricity Act, 2003, all proceedings before the Commission are deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of sections 229 and 267 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,2023 (BNS). The Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV-FC) while recommending Disaster Management Grants has _ inter-alia allocated 10% of the State Disaster Risk Management Fund (SDRMF) and the National Disaster Risk Management Fund (NDRMF) for Preparedness & Capacity Building (P&CB) Sub-window to support the critical institutional, functional and technological components of the disaster management system. XV-FC has further recommended that a separate set of guidelines be developed for Preparedness & Capacity Building (P&CB) funding ~ window. 2. The Disaster Management (DM) Act, 2005 empowers the’ National, State dnd District Disaster Management Authorities to take measures for the prevention of District Disaster Management Authorities to take measures for the prevention of disasters, or the mitigation, or preparedness and capacity building for dealing with the threatening disaster situation or disasters. 4. As per Section 2 (m) of the Disaster Management (DM) Act, 2005, preparedness is the "state of readiness to deal with a threatening disaster situation or disaster and the effects thereof.” 5. Further, as per Section 2 (b) of the DM Act, 2005, Capacity Building includes- -e Identification of existing resources and resources to be acquired or created; e Acquiring or creating resources identified under above sub-clause; © Organization and training of personnel and coordination of such training for effective management of disasters. items.text: INTRODUCTION The livestock sector has evolved into one of the most dynamic and resilient components of Tamil Nadu's economy. Traditionally though it continues to be an important source of livelihood for mill ions of farming families, its significance today extends far beyond the rural economy. The sector contributes significantly to the growth of agriculture, food and nutritional security, value addition, employment, entrepreneurship and the overall economic d evelopment of the State. With changing consumer preferences, rising demand for quality animal products and growing opportunities for processing and exports, livestock has emerged as a rising sector with immense potential for sustained growth. 1 ANIMAL HUSBANDRY DEPARTMENT POLICY NOTE 2026-27 1. INTRODUCTION The livestock sector has evolved into one of the most dynamic and resilient components of Tamil Nadu's economy. Traditionally though it continues to be an important source of livelihood for mill ions of farming families, its significance today extends far beyond the rural economy. The sector contributes significantly to the growth of agriculture, food and nutritional security, value addition, employment, entrepreneurship and the overall economic d evelopment of the State. With changing consumer preferences, rising demand for quality animal products and growing opportunities for processing and exports, livestock has emerged as a rising sector with immense potential for sustained growth. 2 2 One of the defining strengths of the livestock sector is its ability to complement agriculture. It provides a regular and dependable source of income, enables productive utilisation of crop residues and common grazing resources, and helps farmers diversify their income while reducing production risks. Since livestock rearing requires relatively modest land resources, it is accessible to small and marginal farmers as well as landless households, while also offering significant opportunities for commercial farming, producer organisations and private investment across the livestock value chain.

items.text: Since livestock rearing requires relatively modest land resources, it is accessible to small and marginal farmers as well as landless households, while also offering significant opportunities for commercial farming, producer organisations and private investment across the livestock value chain. The economic contribution of the sector to Tamil Nadu is both significant and steadily growing. As per estimates for the year 2024 -25, the livestock sector generated a Gross Value Added*(GVA) of Rs.1,47,495 crore at current *(Source: Estimates of State Domestic Products of Tamil Nadu, Dept. Of Economics & Statistics, 2024-25) 3 prices, contributing 5.10 percent to the Gross State Domestic Product and 39.09 percent of the GVA from agriculture and allied sectors. This sustained growth reflects the increasing importance of livestock as a major contributor to the State's economy. Tamil Nadu is today among the leading producers of livestock products in the Country. During 2024–25, the State produced 114.43 lakh metric tonnes of milk, ranking 11 th nationally. It retained its position as the second -largest producer of eggs, with an annual production** of 2,330.495 crore eggs, and ranked sixth in meat production with an output of 8.02 lakh metric tonnes. The State contributes 4.62 percent of the country's milk production, 15.63 percent of egg production and 7.63 percent of meat production, reflecting the scale and competitiveness of its livestock sector. **(Source: Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025) 3 2 One of the defining strengths of the livestock sector is its ability to complement agriculture.

The per capita availability of milk in Tamil Nadu stands at 407 ml per day, comfortably exceeding the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) recommendation of 300 ml per day. Similarly, annual per capita egg availability has reached 302 eggs, which is more than the minimum recommended level of 180 eggs, demonstrating the sector's vital contribution to nutritional security. Sustained investments by the Departm ent in selective breeding, animal healthcare, fodder development and veterinary infrastructure have been the key factors in driving this growth. Its programmes cover the development of cattle, buffaloes, sheep, goats, pigs and poultry, supported by a strong network of breeding farms, fodder farms and research and training institutions. The Department also undertakes the 5 Quinquennial Livestock Census and annual Integrated Sample Survey, providing reliable data for planning and evidence-based policy making.

Evolution of the Animal Husbandry Department The Animal Husbandry Department has evolved over more than a century into one of the largest and most comprehensive veterinary service delivery systems in the country. Its journey reflects Tamil Nadu's sustained commitment to improved livestock development, disease control, veterinary e ducation and farmer welfare. 10 10 The Civil Veterinary Department was established as a separate department in 1892, marking the beginning of organised veterinary administration in the State. This was followed by the establishment of the Madras Veterinary College in 1903, laying the foundation for formal veterinary education. In 1924, the Hosur Cattle Farm was taken over from the Army and developed into dedicated cattle breeding station, signalling the State's early focus on genetic improvement.

items.text: Recognising the importance of conserving indigenous genetic resources, dedicated research stations were established for Bargur cattle, Pulikulam cattle, Kangayam cattle, Alambadi cattle, goats and Mecheri sheep. Native poultry breeding farms and hatcheries were also established to support conservation and commercial production of indigenous poultry breeds. The Department also broadened its focu s to include animal welfare and responsible animal management. The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Tamil Nadu Amendment) Act, 2017 facilitated the conduct of traditional Jallikattu events under a legal framework. Subsequently, 15 the Tamil Nadu Animal Welfa re Board was constituted, and innovative initiatives such as the Vallalar Palluyir Kappagangal scheme were introduced to mitigate sufferings of abandoned and stray animals on permanent basis. In recent years, veterinary services have become increasingly a ccessible through the expansion of Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU), enabling timely doorstep healthcare for livestock owners across the State. items.text: LIVESTOCK WEALTH IN TAMIL NADU Tamil Nadu is endowed with rich livestock biodiversity and is home to several well - recognised indigenous breeds of cattle, buffaloes, sheep, goats and dogs. Table 1: Indigenous Cattle Breeds of Tamil Nadu S.No Breed Native tract 1 Kangayam Cattle Tiruppur, Erode, Coimbatore and Karur 2 Umblachery Cattle Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Cuddalore 3 Pulikulam Cattle Madurai, Sivagangai, Dindigul, Theni, Virudhunagar and Tirunelveli 4 Bargur Cattle and Buffalo Erode 5 Toda Buffalo The Nilgiris 17 The State is also known for its rich diversity of indigenous sheep breeds, including Mecheri, Ramnad White, Madras Red, Kilakarisal, Vembur, Trichy Black, Coimbatore, Chevvadu, Kachchakatti Black and Nilgiri, each of which is well adapted to the varied agro-climatic conditions of Tamil Nadu. Similarly, the recognised indigenous goat breeds, namely Kanni Adu, Kodi Adu and Salem Black, are widely reared in the southern and western districts of the State. Alongside these indigenous breeds, farmers have successfully adopted high - yielding crossbred dairy cattle to enhance milk production. Jersey crossbreds are predominantly reared in the plains, while Holstein Friesian crossbreds are maintained in suitable agro - climatic regions. Popular goat breeds such as Tellicherry and Jamunapari are also reared for commercial meat production and breeding. 17 16 4.

VETERINARY INSTITUTIONS 6.1 Veterinary Service Delivery The Department pr ovides a comprehensive range of veterinary services, including preventive, curative and diagnostic care, medical and surgical treatment, gynaecological and infertility 22 22 management, deworming, immunisation, disease surveillance and control, artificial insemi nation, fodder development, farmer training and extension services. While specialised veterinary services are delivered by qualified veterinary professionals; minor veterinary care, first aid and breeding support are provided through trained para-veterinary personnel. The veterinary network has expanded significantly from about 120 institutions during the 1960s to 3,813 institutions in 2025 –26, comprising 16 Veterinary Polyclinics, 14 Clinician Centres, 153 Veterinary Hospitals, 2,765 Veterinary Dispensaries and 865 Veterinary Sub - Centres. Besides this, there are 245 Mobile Veterinary Units and 32 Animal Ambulances. 6.1.1 Pattern and Functioning of Veterinary Institutions:  Veterinary Polyclinics are headed by a Clinician and supported by four Veterinary 23 Assistant Surgeons and other staff.

items.text: INSTITUTE OF VETERINARY PREVENTIVE MEDICINE (IVPM), RANIPET The Institute of Veterinary Preventive Medicine is the State's premier institution for the production of veterinary biologicals . The Institute plays a crucial role in protecting livestock and 28 28 poultry health by manufacturing quality vaccines, diagnostic reagents and diluents. A major milestone in the Institute's journey has been the successful upgradation of its vaccine production facilities to comply with the GMP standards prescribed by the Drug Licensing Authority. IVPM is the first Government veterinary biologicals institute in the count ry to achieve this distinction and vaccine production commenced in the new GMP-compliant facility in February 2026. The Institute currently manufactures four bacterial vaccines and five viral vaccines for the prevention and control of major livestock and poultry diseases. These vaccines are supplied to veterinary institutions throughout Tamil Nadu and also cater to the requirements of other States. IVPM also ensures the timely supply of vaccines and diluents required for the implementation of the Pulse Ranikhet Disease Vaccination (RDVK) 29 Programme, contributing significantly to disease prevention in backyard and commercial poultry. Quality remains the cornerstone of the Institute's operations. Every biological product is manufactured under stringent Quality Assurance (QA) and Quality Control (QC) protocols to ensure its safety, potency and efficacy b efore it reaches the field. In addition to vaccine production, IVPM manufactures five diagnostic reagents and one diluent to support disease diagnosis and immunisation programmes. Vaccine production is planned in line with disease prevalence and the vaccination targets under various State and National programmes. The Institute also maintains seed cultures and virulent biological materials that are indispensable for vaccine production, quality assurance and research.

items.text: DISEASE DIAGNOSIS , PREVENTION, CONTROL AND ERADICATION Livestock and poultry are vulnerable to a wide range of bacterial, viral, protozoal and parasitic diseases, which can lead to significant economic losses through reduced productivity, mortality and trade restrictions. Preventing and controlling these diseases is therefore essential not only for protecting farmers' livelihoods but also for improving livestock productivity and enhancing the quality and marketability of Indian livestock and livestock products. 34 34 The Department follows a proactive approach to disease management. Continuous monitoring of disease prevalence and epidemiological trends helps in identifying emerging disease risks and planning appropriate control measures. Early detection through surveillance, timel y reporting by farmers and rapid veterinary intervention plays a vital role in containing disease outbreaks before they spread. Disease prevention remains the cornerstone of the Department's strategy. A comprehensive Disease Control Programme is implemented across the State, with regular vaccination programmes tailored to the endemicity of diseases, prompt containment measures during outbreaks and sustained efforts towards the progressive control and eradication of major livestock and poultry diseases. These activities are supported by a well - established network of disease diagnostic and disease control units across Tamil Nadu, which 35 provide laboratory diagnosis, disease surveillance and technical support, enabling timely and effective response to animal disease outbreaks. 8.1 Diagnostic Units 8.1.1 Veterinary Epidemiology Centre (VEC), Chennai The V eterinary Epidemiology Centre is the nodal institution for disease surveillance, diagnosis, prevention and coordination of animal disease control activities acros s Tamil Nadu. It provides technical guidance to the field veterinary system, supports early disease detection and strengthens the State's preparedness to respond effectively to disease outbreaks.

Key Functions 8.1.1.1 Poultry Farm Inspection and Biosecurity Compliance To strengthen avian disease surveillance and safeguard the poultry sector, the Department undertakes bi -annual inspec tions of private poultry farms to ensure compliance with compartmentalisation guidelines for the prevention and control of Avian Influenza. It also verifies that farms engaged in the export of poultry products adhere to the compartmentalisation principles prescribed by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), with particular emphasis on maintaining robust biosecurity and biosafety standards. 37 8.1.1.2 Stud Bull Disease Monitoring The Centre regularly screens stud bulls maintained at the Department's frozen semen production stations to ensure that only healthy, disease-free animals are used for breeding. It also ensures that frozen semen straws used for artificial insemination are sourced exclusively from disease -free herds, thereby protecting animal health and maintaining the genetic quality and reliability of breeding programmes. 8.1.1.3 Vaccination Monitoring The Veterinary Epidemiology Centre closely monitors the effective implementation of district- level vaccination programmes for achieving optimum vaccination coverage .

By facilitating early disease detection, timely diagnosis and rapid outbreak response, these units play a crucial role in pro tecting animal health, preventing the spread of infectious diseases and minimising economic losses to livestock farmers. 8.1.2.1 Key Functions 8.1.2.1.1 Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance The ADIUs undertake disease diagnosis through systematic collection and laboratory examination of samples from affected animals. Post-mortem examinations are carried out to ascertain the cause of death, and whenever required, samples are referred to specialised 39 laboratories for confirmatory diagnosis. These activities stre ngthen disease surveillance and enable timely detection of emerging and endemic diseases. 8.1.2.1.2 Outbreak Investigation and Control During disease outbreaks, the ADIUs investigate the source, transmission pattern and extent of spread, and recommend appr opriate control and containment measures. They also maintain endemic disease maps and trend analysis, which provide valuable inputs for planning targeted prophylactic vaccination programmes and other preventive interventions.
